# Software Requirements Specification (SRS): Equipment Maintenance Request Portal

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Document | Equipment Maintenance Request Portal — SRS |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Status | Approved for Solution Design |
| Date | 13 October 2026 |
| Owner | Operations Director, Northstar Facilities Group |
| Prepared by | Business Analysis Team |

## 1 Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose

This document defines the functional and non-functional requirements for an equipment maintenance request portal used by Northstar Facilities Group, a fictional company managing commercial office buildings. It provides the requirements for designing and deploying the application on AWS.

### 1.2 Scope

**In scope**
- Submit and track equipment maintenance requests through a web portal.
- Allow maintenance staff to review, assign, and update requests.
- Notify requesters when the status of a request changes.
- Provide an administrative dashboard for request volumes and resolution times.
- Store request records and associated metadata.
- Authenticate users and enforce role-based access.

**Out of scope**
- Native mobile applications.
- Integration with third-party facilities management systems.
- Predictive maintenance and IoT sensor ingestion.
- Automated vendor procurement.
- Multi-Region or multi-AZ deployment during the pilot.

### 1.3 Definitions and acronyms

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| SRS | Software Requirements Specification |
| SLA | Service Level Agreement |
| RBAC | Role-Based Access Control |
| RPO | Recovery Point Objective |
| RTO | Recovery Time Objective |
| AZ | Availability Zone |

### 1.4 References

- Northstar Maintenance Discovery Workshop Notes, 5 October 2026.
- Northstar Information Security Policy, 1 September 2026.
- Northstar Data Retention Policy, 15 August 2026.
- Northstar Operations Reporting Requirements, 7 October 2026.

## 2 Overall description

### 2.1 Product perspective

The portal replaces email-based maintenance requests and manually maintained spreadsheets. It provides a single interface for request submission, work assignment, status tracking, and operational reporting.

The system is a standalone web application. It receives requests from employees, supports processing by maintenance staff, and sends email notifications when defined workflow events occur.

### 2.2 User classes and characteristics

| User class | Headcount | Responsibilities |
|---|---:|---|
| Employees | 500 | Submit requests and track their own requests |
| Maintenance staff | 20 | Review, assign, and resolve requests |
| Operations administrators | 5 | Manage users, view all requests, and generate reports |

### 2.3 Operating environment

The application runs on AWS in the **US East (N. Virginia) Region (`us-east-1`)**, using only **Availability Zone `us-east-1a`**.

The customer explicitly accepts single-AZ availability for this deployment. The system does not require deployment to another Availability Zone or Region.

Users access the application through current versions of Chrome, Edge, and Safari on desktop and mobile browsers.

### 2.4 Design and implementation constraints

- **C-01:** All zonal resources must reside in `us-east-1a`.
- **C-02:** The application must use AWS-native managed services only.
- **C-03:** The application must support HTTPS for all browser communications.
- **C-04:** Access must be controlled through authenticated user roles.
- **C-05:** The monthly AWS infrastructure expenditure must not exceed USD 100.
- **C-06:** The application must not require third-party SaaS services for core request processing.

### 2.5 Assumptions and dependencies

- Employees have access to an internet-connected browser.
- Northstar provides a verified company email domain.
- The customer supplies an administrator account list before deployment.
- Email delivery depends on valid recipient addresses and the availability of the configured email delivery service.
- The customer assigns one operations administrator to manage user access and request categories.

## 3 Functional requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| FR-01 | The system shall allow employees to sign in using company email credentials. | Must |
| FR-02 | The system shall allow employees to submit a request with a title, description, location, category, and priority. | Must |
| FR-03 | The system shall generate a unique request ID for every submitted request. | Must |
| FR-04 | The system shall allow employees to view their own requests and current statuses. | Must |
| FR-05 | The system shall allow maintenance staff to view all open requests. | Must |
| FR-06 | The system shall allow maintenance staff to assign each request to one of 20 maintenance personnel. | Must |
| FR-07 | The system shall support the statuses Submitted, Assigned, In Progress, Resolved, and Closed. | Must |
| FR-08 | The system shall record the timestamp and user identity for every status change. | Must |
| FR-09 | The system shall send an email notification within 60 seconds of a status change. | Must |
| FR-10 | The system shall allow employees to add comments to their own requests. | Should |
| FR-11 | The system shall allow administrators to create, disable, and reactivate user accounts. | Must |
| FR-12 | The system shall provide a dashboard showing request counts by status, category, and priority. | Must |
| FR-13 | The system shall allow administrators to export filtered request records as CSV files. | Should |
| FR-14 | The system shall validate required fields and reject invalid submissions with an explanatory message. | Must |

## 4 Non-functional requirements

| ID | Category | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Volume | The system shall support 525 registered users and 2,000 maintenance requests per month. |
| NFR-02 | Performance | 95% of request submission operations shall complete within 2 seconds under 50 concurrent users. |
| NFR-03 | Performance | 95% of dashboard queries shall complete within 3 seconds for a dataset of 100,000 requests. |
| NFR-04 | Availability | The system shall target 99.0% monthly availability within its single-AZ deployment constraint. |
| NFR-05 | Recovery | The recovery point objective shall be 24 hours, and the recovery time objective shall be 8 hours. |
| NFR-06 | Retention | Request records and audit history shall be retained for 3 years. |
| NFR-07 | Security | All data in transit shall use TLS 1.2 or later, and access shall enforce role-based authorization. |
| NFR-08 | Scalability | The system shall support growth to 10,000 requests per month without changing the user-facing workflow. |
| NFR-09 | Observability | Application errors, failed notifications, and request-processing failures shall be logged and retained for 30 days. |
| NFR-10 | Cost | Total AWS infrastructure expenditure shall remain below USD 100 per month, excluding taxes and employee internet costs. |
| NFR-11 | Compliance | The system shall comply with the customer's information security and data retention policies. |
| NFR-12 | Maintainability | A qualified engineer shall be able to deploy a routine application update within 30 minutes using documented procedures. |

## 5 External interface requirements

| Interface | Integration style | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| Employee browser | HTTPS web interface | Chrome, Edge, and Safari; responsive layout |
| Maintenance staff browser | HTTPS web interface | Request queue, assignment, status updates |
| Administrator browser | HTTPS web interface | User management, reporting, CSV export |
| Company identity | Email and password authentication | Company email identities; no external identity provider required |
| Email delivery | SMTP-compatible email delivery interface | Status notifications; plain-text or HTML email |
| CSV export | Browser file download | UTF-8 CSV; maximum 10,000 records per export |

## 6 Data requirements

| Entity | Description | Indicative volume |
|---|---|---:|
| User | Identity, email, role, and account status | 525 records |
| Maintenance request | Request details, category, priority, status, and timestamps | 24,000 new records annually |
| Assignment | Request-to-maintenance-staff assignment history | 30,000 records annually |
| Comment | User comments associated with requests | 60,000 records annually |
| Audit event | Record of status changes and administrative actions | 100,000 records annually |

- **Growth:** The system shall accommodate 100,000 maintenance requests over its initial operating period.
- **Classification:** User identity and maintenance request data are classified as internal business data.
- **Retention:** Request records, comments, and audit history are retained for 3 years. Expired records shall be deleted within 30 days after the retention period ends.
- **Data integrity:** Every request shall have a unique identifier, creation timestamp, and current status. Audit records shall include the actor, action, and timestamp.

## 7 Acceptance criteria

| ID | Acceptance criterion | Related requirement |
|---|---|---|
| AC-01 | The application shall successfully process a test dataset containing 525 users and 2,000 monthly requests. | NFR-01 |
| AC-02 | At least 95% of 1,000 measured request submissions shall complete within 2 seconds under 50 concurrent users. | NFR-02 |
| AC-03 | At least 95% of dashboard queries shall complete within 3 seconds against 100,000 test requests. | NFR-03 |
| AC-04 | A 30-day monitoring test shall demonstrate at least 99.0% measured availability, excluding planned maintenance. | NFR-04 |
| AC-05 | A recovery exercise shall restore data to a point no older than 24 hours and restore service within 8 hours. | NFR-05 |
| AC-06 | A retention test shall confirm that expired records are deleted within 30 days of the 3-year retention period ending. | NFR-06 |
| AC-07 | Security testing shall confirm HTTPS enforcement and prevent users from accessing records outside their authorized roles. | NFR-07 |
| AC-08 | A load test shall demonstrate 10,000 requests per month without changes to the user-facing workflow. | NFR-08 |
| AC-09 | Injected processing failures shall appear in application logs within 60 seconds and remain available for 30 days. | NFR-09 |
| AC-10 | The monthly infrastructure cost estimate shall remain below USD 100 at the specified baseline workload. | NFR-10 |
| AC-11 | A compliance review shall verify the required access controls and retention rules. | NFR-11 |
| AC-12 | An engineer following the deployment guide shall complete a routine application update within 30 minutes. | NFR-12 |

## 8 Open issues

| ID | Issue | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Confirm the final list of maintenance request categories before configuration. | Operations Director |
| OI-02 | Confirm the company email domain and sender verification requirements. | IT Administrator |
| OI-03 | Approve the backup and recovery procedure for the single-AZ deployment. | IT Administrator |
| OI-04 | Confirm whether CSV exports require additional approval for records exceeding 5,000 rows. | Operations Director |

# Landing zone spec: Northstar Facilities Group

Status: **ready** (landing zone 1)

## Summary

Minimal landing zone for Northstar Facilities Group: 4 OUs and 5 accounts, standalone VPCs, local-nat egress, home region us-east-1; prod 1 AZ, nonprod 1 AZ.

## Tier and why

- Tier: **minimal** [explicit: Multi-Region or multi-AZ deployment during the pilot]
- Mode: greenfield [inferred: No existing AWS Organization or Control Tower deployment is mentioned; greenfield is the correct starting point]

## Organization

| OU | Role | Parent | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Security | security | root | default: Control Tower hub OU for Log Archive and Audit accounts |
| Workloads | workloads | root | default: workload OU |
| Prod | prod | Workloads | default: production environment |
| NonProd | nonprod | Workloads | default: non-production environment |

| Account | Kind | OU | Environment | Provisioning | Baseline services |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| northstar-management | management | root | - | existing | organizations, control-tower, identity-center |
| Log Archive | log-archive | Security | - | control-tower | cloudtrail, config, log-bucket |
| Audit | audit | Security | - | control-tower | security-hub, guardduty, access-analyzer |
| northstar-maintenance-portal-prod | workload | Prod | prod | account-factory | - |
| northstar-maintenance-portal-nonprod | workload | NonProd | nonprod | account-factory | - |

## Regions

- Home: us-east-1
- Governed: us-east-1
- Allowed (governed + extra): us-east-1
- Region deny: Control Tower control CT.MULTISERVICE.PV.1 on every top-level OU

## Identity

- Source: identity-center-directory (IAM Identity Center (built-in directory))
- Delegated administration: management account
- Break-glass users: yes
- Basis: explicit: Company email identities; no external identity provider required

## Logging

- Retention: 365 days (access logs 3650 days)
- Encryption: sse-s3
- Also centralized: none

## Security services

- guardduty, delegated to Audit [default: SRA: security tooling account]
- security-hub, delegated to Audit [default: SRA: security tooling account]
- access-analyzer, delegated to Audit [default: SRA: security tooling account]

## Network

- Connectivity: none
- Egress: local-nat through northstar-maintenance-portal-prod
- Ingress: distributed, WAF per-workload
- Inspection: none
- Endpoints: per-vpc
- DNS: vpc-default
- Hybrid: none
- IPAM: off (top range 10.0.0.0/8)
- Evidence connectivity: inferred: Minimal tier with a single workload and no on-premises link; standalone VPCs with no inter-VPC routing required
- Evidence egress.model: inferred: Minimal tier; local NAT gateway per VPC is sufficient for a single workload with no central inspection requirement
- Evidence ingress.model: inferred: Internet-facing web portal accessed by browser users; distributed ALB per workload is the default
- Evidence inspection.model: inferred: No outbound inspection or east-west segmentation requirement stated in the SRS
- Evidence endpoints.model: inferred: Single VPC per environment; per-VPC gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB are sufficient
- Evidence hybrid.type: explicit: Multi-Region or multi-AZ deployment during the pilot
- Evidence dns: inferred: No hybrid DNS or shared resolver requirement; VPC default DNS resolver is sufficient
- Evidence ipam.enabled: inferred: Minimal tier with two standalone VPCs; IPAM is not required

| VPC | Account | Region | Purpose | CIDR | AZs | Tiers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wl_prod_use1 | northstar-maintenance-portal-prod | us-east-1 | workload | 10.0.0.0/20 | us-east-1a | public, private-app, private-data |
| wl_nonprod_use1 | northstar-maintenance-portal-nonprod | us-east-1 | workload | 10.0.16.0/20 | us-east-1a | public, private-app, private-data |

| Environment | Account | Region | AZs | DR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prod | northstar-maintenance-portal-prod | us-east-1 | 1 | none |
| nonprod | northstar-maintenance-portal-nonprod | us-east-1 | 1 | none |

## Guardrails

Service control policies:
- `deny-leave-org` on root
- `deny-root-user` on Workloads
- `protect-audit-trail` on Workloads
- `deny-guardduty-disable` on Workloads

Control Tower controls:
- `AWS-GR_RESTRICT_ROOT_USER` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_RESTRICT_ROOT_USER_ACCESS_KEYS` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_ROOT_ACCOUNT_MFA_ENABLED` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_ENCRYPTED_VOLUMES` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_RDS_INSTANCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_RDS_SNAPSHOTS_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_RDS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTED` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_READ_PROHIBITED` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_WRITE_PROHIBITED` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_RESTRICTED_COMMON_PORTS` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_RESTRICTED_SSH` on Workloads
- `AWS-GR_AUDIT_BUCKET_RETENTION_POLICY` on Workloads

Custom SCP intents (written as policy JSON by the IaC step, for review):
- `deny-high-cost-services` on Workloads: Deny provisioning of services that would breach the USD 100/month infrastructure budget cap, including large EC2 instance families, Redshift, EMR, and other high-cost managed services not required by the portal workload.

## Platform contract per environment

### prod

```
environment: prod
account: northstar-maintenance-portal-prod (OU Workloads/Prod)
region: us-east-1  # design.region must equal this
vpc: wl_prod_use1 10.0.0.0/20, 1 AZs: us-east-1a
subnet tiers (pre-filled boundaries; place zonal components in these, never add tiers):
  - vpc_prod_public: public 10.0.0.0/24
  - vpc_prod_private_app: private-app 10.0.1.0/24
  - vpc_prod_private_data: private-data 10.0.2.0/24
dr: none  # no DR region; recovery is in-region (multi-AZ and backups)
connectivity: none
egress: local-nat  # one NAT Gateway per AZ in the public tier for production, one in total for non-production
ingress: distributed, waf: per-workload  # the public entry point (ALB, and WAF when listed) lives in this VPC's public tier
endpoints: per-vpc; S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints are always per VPC
hybrid: none
provided_by_platform (never add these as components): AWS CloudTrail, AWS Config, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, AWS IAM Access Analyzer, AWS IAM Identity Center
workload_owns: public entry point (ALB, WAF), KMS keys for its data, CloudWatch logs and alarms, AWS Backup plans, application IAM roles
```

### nonprod

```
environment: nonprod
account: northstar-maintenance-portal-nonprod (OU Workloads/NonProd)
region: us-east-1  # design.region must equal this
vpc: wl_nonprod_use1 10.0.16.0/20, 1 AZs: us-east-1a
subnet tiers (pre-filled boundaries; place zonal components in these, never add tiers):
  - vpc_nonprod_public: public 10.0.16.0/24
  - vpc_nonprod_private_app: private-app 10.0.17.0/24
  - vpc_nonprod_private_data: private-data 10.0.18.0/24
dr: none  # no DR region; recovery is in-region (multi-AZ and backups)
connectivity: none
egress: local-nat  # one NAT Gateway per AZ in the public tier for production, one in total for non-production
ingress: distributed, waf: per-workload  # the public entry point (ALB, and WAF when listed) lives in this VPC's public tier
endpoints: per-vpc; S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints are always per VPC
hybrid: none
provided_by_platform (never add these as components): AWS CloudTrail, AWS Config, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, AWS IAM Access Analyzer, AWS IAM Identity Center
workload_owns: public entry point (ALB, WAF), KMS keys for its data, CloudWatch logs and alarms, AWS Backup plans, application IAM roles
```

## Assumptions

- No existing AWS Organization or Control Tower deployment exists for Northstar Facilities Group; this is a net-new greenfield landing zone. (The SRS makes no reference to an existing AWS account structure, Organization, or Control Tower.)
- The 30-day log retention stated in NFR-09 applies to application-level logs (CloudWatch Logs). The landing-zone CloudTrail and AWS Config logs in Log Archive are retained for the default 365 days. (NFR-09 specifies 30 days for application errors and processing failures; no shorter retention is stated for audit/compliance logs.)
- The RTO of 8 hours and RPO of 24 hours (NFR-05) are met by AWS Backup snapshots within the single us-east-1 Region. No DR region or second VPC is required. (The SRS explicitly excludes multi-Region deployment during the pilot and the RTO/RPO targets are achievable with in-Region snapshot restore; drStrategy is therefore set to none at the landing-zone level.)
- SSE-S3 (AWS-managed keys) is sufficient for log encryption. No customer-managed KMS key is required. (The SRS does not mention key management requirements, KMS, or a regulated framework (PCI DSS, HIPAA, etc.) that would mandate customer-managed keys.)
- The non-production account covers both development and testing stages. No separate Dev or Test OU is needed because the SRS states no different policies per stage. (The SRS defines a single non-production environment with no policy differentiation between dev and test.)
- The workload uses AWS-native managed services (Cognito or IAM Identity Center for app auth, RDS or DynamoDB, SES, Lambda/ECS, ALB) consistent with C-02. The landing zone does not prescribe specific services. (C-02 mandates AWS-native managed services only; the landing zone provides the account and network scaffold.)

## Open questions

- OI-01 (from SRS): Confirm the final list of maintenance request categories before portal configuration.
- OI-02 (from SRS): Confirm the company email domain and SES sender verification requirements for status notifications.
- OI-03 (from SRS): Approve the backup and recovery procedure for the single-AZ deployment (RTO 8 h / RPO 24 h via AWS Backup snapshot restore).
- OI-04 (from SRS): Confirm whether CSV exports exceeding 5,000 rows require additional approval.
- LZ-01: Confirm the AWS account email addresses to be used for the management, Log Archive, Audit, prod workload, and nonprod workload accounts.
- LZ-02: Confirm whether a separate sandbox account is needed for engineers to experiment with AWS services without impacting the cost cap on the workload accounts.
- LZ-03: Confirm whether the USD 100/month cost cap applies per account or across the entire organization, to determine whether AWS Budgets alerts should be set at account or org level.

## Flags for review

Nothing here caused a model call. Tick a flag in the Revise section to add its instruction.

Answer:

Answer:

## Designed, not codified

The network (VPCs, Transit Gateways, IPAM, egress, inspection, endpoints, DNS, hybrid links), IAM Identity Center, the security services and AWS Backup are designed here but not codified by the landing-zone IaC; the IaC lists them under "Not codified".
- All zonal resources must reside in us-east-1a (C-01): Control Tower and AWS Organizations infrastructure (CloudTrail, Config, IAM Identity Center) is regional and cannot be constrained to a single AZ. The workload VPC subnets will be placed in us-east-1a per the workload architect's design, but the landing zone itself cannot enforce a single-AZ constraint at the platform level.

# Architecture Decision Record: Equipment Maintenance Request Portal

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Customer | Northstar Facilities Group |
| Status | Proposed |
| Date | 2026-10-30 |
| Region | us-east-1 |
| Availability Zones | us-east-1a |
| DR Region | None |
| Source document | srs.md |
| Components | 15 |

## 1. Context

Northstar Facilities Group manages commercial office buildings and currently handles equipment maintenance requests via email and spreadsheets. This portal replaces that process with a web application supporting 525 users (employees, maintenance staff, and administrators) across request submission, assignment, status tracking, email notifications, and operational reporting. The system runs in a single AZ (us-east-1a) by explicit customer choice, targets 99.0% monthly availability, must stay within USD 100/month, and must retain all request records and audit history for 3 years. No external identity provider is required; no DR Region is provisioned.

## 2. Requirements addressed

| ID | Requirement | Type |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-01 | The system shall allow employees to sign in using company email credentials with role-based access control. | functional |
| REQ-02 | The system shall allow employees to submit, view, and comment on maintenance requests with title, description, location, category, and priority. | functional |
| REQ-03 | The system shall generate a unique request ID for every submitted request and record timestamps and user identity for every status change. | functional |
| REQ-04 | The system shall allow maintenance staff to view all open requests, assign them to personnel, and update statuses through the workflow: Submitted, Assigned, In Progress, Resolved, Closed. | functional |
| REQ-05 | The system shall send an email notification within 60 seconds of a status change. | functional |
| REQ-06 | The system shall provide a dashboard showing request counts by status, category, and priority, and allow administrators to export filtered records as UTF-8 CSV files (up to 10,000 records). | functional |
| REQ-07 | The system shall allow administrators to create, disable, and reactivate user accounts. | functional |
| REQ-08 | The system shall support 525 registered users and 2,000 maintenance requests per month, with a growth path to 10,000 requests per month. | non_functional |
| REQ-09 | 95% of request submission operations shall complete within 2 seconds under 50 concurrent users. | non_functional |
| REQ-10 | 95% of dashboard queries shall complete within 3 seconds for a dataset of 100,000 requests. | non_functional |
| REQ-11 | The system shall target 99.0% monthly availability within a single-AZ deployment in us-east-1a. | non_functional |
| REQ-12 | The recovery point objective shall be 24 hours and the recovery time objective shall be 8 hours. | non_functional |
| REQ-13 | Request records, comments, and audit history shall be retained for 3 years; expired records shall be deleted within 30 days after the retention period ends. | non_functional |
| REQ-14 | All data in transit shall use TLS 1.2 or later and access shall enforce role-based authorization. | non_functional |
| REQ-15 | Total AWS infrastructure expenditure shall remain below USD 100 per month. | constraint |
| REQ-16 | All zonal resources must reside in us-east-1a; the application must use AWS-native managed services only; no third-party SaaS for core request processing. | constraint |
| REQ-17 | Application errors, failed notifications, and request-processing failures shall be logged and retained for 30 days. | non_functional |
| REQ-18 | A qualified engineer shall be able to deploy a routine application update within 30 minutes using documented procedures. | non_functional |

## 3. Architecture decisions

### ADR-001: Use AWS Fargate (single task) for the application API and web serving

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The portal serves 525 users with at most 50 concurrent users (REQ-08, REQ-09). The SRS mandates a single-AZ deployment (REQ-11, REQ-16) and a USD 100/month cost ceiling (REQ-15). A long-running web/API service with persistent HTTP connections is needed. The deployment must be updatable within 30 minutes (REQ-18).

**Decision:** Use one AWS Fargate task (Linux/ARM64, 0.5 vCPU / 1 GB) in the private-app subnet of us-east-1a. A single task is sufficient for the stated concurrency; the ECS service can scale to additional tasks if load grows. Container images are stored in Amazon ECR.

**Consequences:**
- Graviton ARM64 minimises compute cost, keeping the design within the USD 100 budget.
- A single task means no redundancy within the AZ; a task failure causes a brief outage until ECS restarts it (consistent with the 99.0% availability target).
- Scaling to 10,000 requests/month (REQ-08) is achieved by increasing the desired task count without workflow changes.
- Deployments via ECS rolling update satisfy the 30-minute update requirement (REQ-18).

**Requirements:** REQ-08, REQ-09, REQ-11, REQ-15, REQ-16, REQ-18

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** AWS Lambda for the API (Lambda cold starts and the 15-minute execution limit are unsuitable for a stateful web session and streaming CSV exports up to 10,000 rows (REQ-06); Lambda would also require API Gateway, adding cost.); Amazon EC2 t4g.micro (EC2 requires OS patching and AMI management, violating the managed-services constraint (REQ-16), and a t4g.micro has only 1 GiB RAM which is the same as the Fargate task but with higher operational overhead.)

### ADR-002: Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ for request and audit data

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The data model is relational: requests, assignments, comments, and audit events require joins and transactions (REQ-03, REQ-10). The dashboard must query 100,000 records within 3 seconds (REQ-10). The SRS mandates single-AZ deployment (REQ-16) and a 24-hour RPO / 8-hour RTO (REQ-12). The cost ceiling is USD 100/month (REQ-15).

**Decision:** Use one Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 Single-AZ instance, db.t4g.micro, gp3 20 GiB, 7-day automated backups with point-in-time recovery, encrypted with the customer managed KMS key, placed in the private-data subnet of us-east-1a.

**Consequences:**
- Automated daily snapshots and PITR satisfy the 24-hour RPO; restoring a snapshot to a new instance satisfies the 8-hour RTO.
- Single-AZ means a hardware failure requires a snapshot restore, which is accepted per the 99.0% availability target and customer sign-off.
- db.t4g.micro (2 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM) is the smallest Graviton RDS size; move to db.t4g.small when average CPU exceeds 70% or free memory drops below 200 MiB.
- PostgreSQL full-text search and window functions satisfy the dashboard query requirement without a separate analytics service.

**Requirements:** REQ-03, REQ-10, REQ-12, REQ-13, REQ-15, REQ-16

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Amazon DynamoDB (Dashboard queries (REQ-10) require aggregations and joins across requests, assignments, and audit events that are natural in SQL but expensive to model in DynamoDB.); Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 (Aurora's minimum cost (0.5 ACU minimum) exceeds the db.t4g.micro price and would push the design over the USD 100 budget (REQ-15).)

### ADR-003: Use Amazon Cognito for user authentication and RBAC

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The portal requires email-and-password sign-in for 525 users with three roles (employee, maintenance staff, administrator) and no external identity provider (REQ-01, REQ-07, REQ-14). The solution must use AWS-native managed services (REQ-16).

**Decision:** Use one Amazon Cognito user pool (Essentials tier) with email-and-password authentication. Three Cognito groups map to the three application roles. The application validates the JWT issued by Cognito on every API request to enforce RBAC.

**Consequences:**
- Cognito's free tier (50,000 MAUs) covers the 525-user base at zero incremental cost, supporting the USD 100 budget.
- Administrators manage user accounts (create, disable, reactivate) via the Cognito admin API called from the application (REQ-07).
- Password reset and account recovery are handled natively by Cognito, reducing application code.
- If Northstar later requires SAML federation, Cognito supports it without replacing the authentication layer.

**Requirements:** REQ-01, REQ-07, REQ-14, REQ-16

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Custom JWT authentication in the application (Building and maintaining a secure credential store violates the managed-services constraint (REQ-16) and introduces security risk.)

### ADR-004: Use Amazon SES for email status notifications

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The system must send email notifications within 60 seconds of a status change (REQ-05). The SRS requires an AWS-native service and no third-party SaaS (REQ-16). The customer provides a verified company email domain (Section 2.5).

**Decision:** Use Amazon SES with one verified domain identity and DKIM enabled. The application API calls SES directly via the AWS SDK on each status-change event. SES delivery failures are logged to CloudWatch.

**Consequences:**
- SES sends email within seconds of the API call, satisfying the 60-second notification requirement.
- SES sandbox mode must be exited before go-live; the customer must verify the sending domain (OI-02).
- SES is a regional service with no VPC placement required; the Fargate task reaches it via the NAT Gateway.
- Bounces and complaints are handled via SES event notifications to CloudWatch.

**Requirements:** REQ-05, REQ-16

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Amazon SNS email subscriptions (SNS email is intended for operational alerts, not transactional application notifications; it does not support HTML templates or per-recipient personalisation needed for status notifications.)

### ADR-005: Use Application Load Balancer with AWS WAF as the public entry point

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The platform contract mandates a per-workload WAF and a distributed ingress pattern with the ALB in the public tier (ingress: distributed, waf: per-workload). All browser communications must use HTTPS (REQ-14, C-03). The ALB terminates TLS and forwards to the Fargate task.

**Decision:** Deploy one internet-facing Application Load Balancer (single_az in us-east-1a, the only AZ in this deployment) with an HTTPS 443 listener and an ACM certificate. Attach one AWS WAF web ACL (AWS managed Core Rule Set, Known Bad Inputs, and one rate-based rule) to the ALB.

**Consequences:**
- TLS termination at the ALB enforces HTTPS for all browser traffic (REQ-14).
- WAF protects against common web exploits and rate-based abuse without additional cost beyond the WAF ACL and rule charges.
- The ALB and WAF are the only components in the public subnet; all application and data resources remain private.
- ALB access logs provide an audit trail of all inbound requests.

**Requirements:** REQ-14, REQ-15, REQ-16

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Amazon API Gateway HTTP API (API Gateway adds per-request cost and is optimised for REST/HTTP APIs rather than serving a full web application with file downloads and session-based flows; ALB is more cost-effective at this scale.)

### ADR-006: Use Amazon S3 for CSV exports and static assets with lifecycle retention

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** Administrators export filtered request records as CSV files up to 10,000 rows (REQ-06). Request records and audit history must be retained for 3 years and deleted within 30 days after expiry (REQ-13). A cost-effective object store is needed (REQ-15).

**Decision:** Use one Amazon S3 bucket for CSV exports and application static assets. Enable SSE-KMS encryption, versioning, and Block Public Access. Apply an S3 lifecycle rule to transition objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days and expire them after 3 years plus 30 days (1,125 days total).

**Consequences:**
- Lifecycle rules automate the 3-year retention and 30-day deletion window (REQ-13) without manual intervention.
- Pre-signed URLs generated by the API allow secure browser downloads without making the bucket public.
- S3 Standard storage cost for the expected export volume is negligible within the USD 100 budget.
- Glacier transition reduces long-term storage cost for aged exports.

**Requirements:** REQ-06, REQ-13, REQ-15

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Serving CSV directly from the database via the API response stream (Streaming large exports through the Fargate task ties up the task for the duration of the download and does not provide durable storage or audit of exported files.)

### ADR-007: Use AWS Backup for automated database snapshots to meet RPO/RTO

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The RPO is 24 hours and the RTO is 8 hours (REQ-12). The deployment is single-AZ with no DR Region (REQ-16, contract). The customer must approve the backup and recovery procedure (OI-03).

**Decision:** Use AWS Backup with a daily backup plan targeting the RDS instance, a 7-day retention window in the primary vault, and a backup window of 02:00–03:00 UTC. RDS automated backups (7-day retention, PITR) are also enabled as a secondary recovery path.

**Consequences:**
- Daily snapshots satisfy the 24-hour RPO; restoring a snapshot to a new db.t4g.micro instance in us-east-1a satisfies the 8-hour RTO.
- AWS Backup provides centralised visibility and policy-driven compliance reporting for OI-03.
- Snapshot storage cost is minimal for a 20 GiB database.
- A hardware failure in the single AZ requires a restore; there is no automatic failover.

**Requirements:** REQ-12, REQ-13, REQ-15

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** RDS automated backups only (no AWS Backup) (AWS Backup provides a centralised audit trail and policy enforcement required by the customer's information security policy (NFR-11); RDS automated backups alone do not satisfy the compliance reporting need.)

## 4. Network layout

The solution runs in AWS Region us-east-1. It uses one VPC, Prod VPC, in Availability Zone us-east-1a. The Public subnets (public) use 10.0.0.0/24 in us-east-1a. The App subnets (private-app) use 10.0.1.0/24 in us-east-1a. The Data subnets (private-data) use 10.0.2.0/24 in us-east-1a. The Prod VPC contains the VPC Endpoints. The Public subnets, in Prod VPC, contains the Web Application Firewall, the Application Load Balancer and the NAT Gateway. The App subnets, in Prod VPC, contains the Portal API. The Data subnets, in Prod VPC, contains the Request Database. Region-level services used: Container Registry, User Pool, Export and Assets Bucket, Email Notification Service, Backup Plan, Encryption Key, Secrets Store and Observability. Outside AWS, the solution involves: Portal Users.

### Platform contract

The approved landing zone fixes these values; the design places its components inside them.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Account | northstar-maintenance-portal-prod |
| Organizational unit | Workloads/Prod |
| Region | us-east-1 |
| Availability Zones | us-east-1a |
| Prod VPC | 10.0.0.0/20 (us-east-1) |
| Public subnets (public) | 10.0.0.0/24 |
| App subnets (private-app) | 10.0.1.0/24 |
| Data subnets (private-data) | 10.0.2.0/24 |
| DR Region | None |
| Connectivity | none |
| Egress | local-nat |
| Ingress | distributed, WAF per-workload |
| Provided by the platform | AWS CloudTrail, AWS Config, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, AWS IAM Access Analyzer, AWS IAM Identity Center |
| Landing-zone version | version 1 (f9fff5e1fd38f60b) |

## 5. Components

| ID | Component | AWS service | SKU / configuration | Qty | Placement | AZ placement | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-00 | Portal Users | Users (Employees, Maintenance Staff, Administrators) | 525 users across three roles | 1 | External | External | Employees submit and track requests; maintenance staff assign and resolve requests; administrators manage users and generate reports. |
| C-01 | Web Application Firewall | AWS WAF | 1 web ACL, Core Rule Set + Known Bad Inputs + 1 rate-based rule, attached to ALB | 1 | Public subnets | Single AZ (us-east-1a) | Protects the public entry point against common web exploits and rate-based abuse as required by the platform contract. |
| C-02 | Application Load Balancer | Application Load Balancer | Internet-facing ALB, HTTPS 443, ACM certificate, targets Fargate tasks | 1 | Public subnets | Single AZ (us-east-1a) | Terminates TLS and forwards HTTPS requests from browsers to the Portal API Fargate task. |
| C-03 | NAT Gateway | NAT Gateway | 1 public NAT Gateway in us-east-1a | 1 | Public subnets | Single AZ (us-east-1a) | Provides outbound internet access for the Fargate task to reach Amazon SES and other AWS regional endpoints not covered by VPC gateway endpoints. |
| C-04 | Portal API | AWS Fargate | Fargate Linux/ARM64, 0.5 vCPU / 1 GB, 1 task in us-east-1a | 1 | App subnets | Single AZ (us-east-1a) | Runs the stateless web application and REST API: handles request submission, status updates, assignment, comments, user management, dashboard queries, and CSV export generation. |
| C-05 | Container Registry | Amazon ECR | Private ECR repository, scan on push, lifecycle keeps last 10 images | 1 | Region | Regional | Stores and versions the Portal API container image used by the ECS service. |
| C-06 | User Pool | Amazon Cognito | Cognito user pool, Essentials tier, email/password auth, 3 groups | 1 | Region | Regional | Authenticates all 525 users with email and password, issues JWTs, and enforces role-based access via Cognito groups for employee, maintenance staff, and administrator roles. |
| C-07 | Request Database | Amazon RDS | db.t4g.micro, PostgreSQL 17, gp3 20 GiB, Single-AZ, 7-day backups | 1 | Data subnets | Single AZ (us-east-1a) | System of record for all maintenance requests, assignments, comments, audit events, and user data; supports dashboard aggregation queries and CSV export filtering. |
| C-08 | Export and Assets Bucket | Amazon S3 | S3 Standard, SSE-KMS, versioning on, lifecycle to Glacier at 90 days, expiry at 1125 days | 1 | Region | Regional | Stores administrator CSV exports (served via pre-signed URLs) and application static assets; lifecycle rules enforce the 3-year retention and 30-day deletion window. |
| C-09 | Email Notification Service | Amazon SES | SES verified domain identity, DKIM on, shared IP, 1 configuration set | 1 | Region | Regional | Delivers transactional email notifications to requesters within 60 seconds of a status change event triggered by the Portal API. |
| C-10 | Backup Plan | AWS Backup | AWS Backup daily plan, 7-day retention, targeting RDS instance | 1 | Region | Regional | Provides centralised, policy-driven daily snapshots of the RDS instance to satisfy the 24-hour RPO and compliance reporting requirements. |
| C-11 | Encryption Key | AWS KMS | 1 customer managed symmetric KMS key, annual rotation | 1 | Region | Regional | Encrypts the RDS database and S3 bucket at rest with a customer managed key, satisfying the information security policy. |
| C-12 | Secrets Store | AWS Secrets Manager | 1 secret for RDS credentials, automatic rotation every 30 days | 1 | Region | Regional | Stores and rotates the RDS master credentials used by the Portal API, eliminating hard-coded secrets. |
| C-13 | Observability | Amazon CloudWatch | CloudWatch log groups (30-day retention), 1 dashboard, alarms on errors and saturation | 1 | Region | Regional | Collects application logs, ECS task metrics, and RDS metrics; raises alarms on errors, failed notifications, and resource saturation; provides the operational dashboard. |
| C-14 | VPC Endpoints | AWS PrivateLink | S3 gateway endpoint for the Prod VPC | 1 | Prod VPC | Regional | Routes S3 traffic from the Fargate task and RDS backups through the S3 gateway endpoint, avoiding NAT Gateway data charges for S3 access. |

## 6. Request and data flow

1. Portal Users send HTTPS requests to the Application Load Balancer on port 443. (F-01; HTTPS 443)
2. The Application Load Balancer passes all inbound requests through the Web Application Firewall before forwarding them. (F-02; HTTPS 443)
3. The Application Load Balancer forwards inspected HTTPS requests to the Portal API Fargate task on port 8080. (F-03; HTTP 8080)
4. The Portal API validates Cognito-issued JWTs against the User Pool to authenticate and authorise every request. (F-04; HTTPS 443)
5. The Portal API retrieves RDS credentials from the Secrets Store at startup and on rotation. (F-05; HTTPS 443)
6. The Portal API reads and writes maintenance requests, assignments, comments, and audit events in the Request Database. (F-06; PostgreSQL 5432)
7. The Portal API calls the Email Notification Service via the AWS SDK to send status-change emails to requesters. (F-07; HTTPS 443)
8. The Portal API writes generated CSV export files to the Export and Assets Bucket and returns a pre-signed URL to the administrator. (F-08; HTTPS 443)
9. Portal Users (administrators) download CSV export files directly from the Export and Assets Bucket using a pre-signed URL. (F-09; HTTPS 443)
10. The Backup Plan takes a daily snapshot of the Request Database and stores it in the AWS Backup vault. (F-10; AWS internal N/A)
11. The Portal API emits application logs and custom metrics to Observability (CloudWatch) for error tracking and alerting. (F-11; HTTPS 443)

## 7. Security and operations

- All inbound traffic enters exclusively through the Application Load Balancer (C-02) on port 443; the WAF (C-01) inspects every request before it reaches the Portal API (C-04). Security groups allow port 443 inbound only from 0.0.0.0/0 on the ALB; the Portal API security group allows port 8080 only from the ALB security group; the Request Database security group allows port 5432 only from the Portal API security group.
- All data at rest is encrypted: the Request Database (C-07) and Export and Assets Bucket (C-08) use the customer managed KMS key (C-11) via SSE-KMS. S3 Block Public Access is enabled on C-08.
- All data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or higher: HTTPS is enforced at the ALB (C-02); the Portal API (C-04) communicates with AWS services over TLS; the RDS connection uses SSL with certificate verification.
- The Portal API (C-04) runs under a least-privilege IAM role scoped to: read from Secrets Manager (C-12), send email via SES (C-09), read/write the S3 bucket (C-08), and write CloudWatch logs (C-13). No wildcard actions or resource ARNs are permitted.
- RDS master credentials are stored in Secrets Manager (C-12) with automatic rotation every 30 days. No long-lived access keys are used anywhere in the workload.
- Amazon Cognito (C-06) issues short-lived JWTs; the Portal API validates the token signature and group membership on every API call to enforce RBAC across employee, maintenance staff, and administrator roles.
- CloudWatch (C-13) retains all application and infrastructure logs for 30 days. Alarms are configured on application error rates, failed SES notifications, ECS task CPU and memory, and RDS CPU and free storage.
- AWS CloudTrail (provided by platform) records all API calls across the account. The S3 gateway endpoint (C-14) ensures S3 traffic does not traverse the public internet.
- The ECR repository (C-05) has scan-on-push enabled; critical vulnerabilities must be remediated before deploying a new image. The ECS task definition uses read-only root filesystem and drops all Linux capabilities not required by the application.
- AWS Backup (C-10) enforces a backup vault lock policy preventing deletion of snapshots within the 7-day retention window, supporting the RPO of 24 hours and the customer's information security policy.

## 8. Assumptions

| ID | Assumption | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| ASM-01 | The Portal API container listens on port 8080 and the ALB target group is configured accordingly. | The SRS does not specify an application port; 8080 is the conventional non-privileged HTTP port for containerised web applications. |
| ASM-02 | MFA is optional (not enforced) in the Cognito user pool. | The SRS requires email-and-password authentication (Section 5) but does not mandate MFA; optional MFA allows administrators to enable it later without a design change. |
| ASM-03 | The RDS instance uses db.t4g.micro (2 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM), the smallest Graviton RDS size. | The SRS data volumes (525 users, 100,000 requests over the operating period) are modest; db.t4g.micro is the most cost-effective choice to stay within the USD 100/month budget (REQ-15). Upgrade to db.t4g.small when average CPU exceeds 70% or free memory drops below 200 MiB. |
| ASM-04 | The Fargate task uses 0.5 vCPU and 1 GB memory, the smallest valid Fargate configuration. | 50 concurrent users (REQ-09) with a stateless API is well within the capacity of a single small Fargate task; this minimises cost (REQ-15). |
| ASM-05 | SES is used in the us-east-1 region and the customer will exit SES sandbox mode before go-live. | SES sandbox mode restricts sending to verified addresses only; production use requires sandbox exit, which depends on the customer verifying their domain (OI-02). |
| ASM-06 | The S3 lifecycle expiration is set to 1,125 days (3 years × 365 days + 30 days grace period) to satisfy the retention and deletion requirements. | REQ-13 requires 3-year retention and deletion within 30 days after expiry; 1,125 days covers both without manual intervention. |
| ASM-07 | The ACM certificate for the ALB is issued for the customer's domain and managed by ACM for automatic renewal. | The SRS requires HTTPS (C-03) but does not specify the domain name; ACM-managed certificates eliminate manual renewal overhead. |
| ASM-08 | No ElastiCache or query caching layer is added for dashboard queries. | PostgreSQL with appropriate indexes on a db.t4g.micro can satisfy the 3-second dashboard query target (REQ-10) for 100,000 records; a cache would add cost that risks breaching the USD 100 budget (REQ-15). |

## 9. Open questions

- OI-01 (from SRS): The final list of maintenance request categories must be confirmed by the Operations Director before application configuration.
- OI-02 (from SRS): The company email domain and SES sender verification requirements must be confirmed by the IT Administrator before go-live; SES sandbox exit depends on this.
- OI-03 (from SRS): The IT Administrator must formally approve the single-AZ backup and recovery procedure, including the expected 8-hour RTO via snapshot restore.
- OI-04 (from SRS): The Operations Director must confirm whether CSV exports exceeding 5,000 rows require additional approval, as this may require an application-level workflow gate.
- The ACM certificate domain name has not been specified in the SRS; the customer must provide the DNS name for the portal before the ALB listener can be configured.
- The SRS does not specify whether the Cognito user pool should enforce password complexity beyond AWS defaults; the customer's information security policy (NFR-11) should be reviewed to confirm.

design.json.data:
{
  "title": "Equipment Maintenance Request Portal",
  "customer": "Northstar Facilities Group",
  "context": "Northstar Facilities Group manages commercial office buildings and currently handles equipment maintenance requests via email and spreadsheets. This portal replaces that process with a web application supporting 525 users (employees, maintenance staff, and administrators) across request submission, assignment, status tracking, email notifications, and operational reporting. The system runs in a single AZ (us-east-1a) by explicit customer choice, targets 99.0% monthly availability, must stay within USD 100/month, and must retain all request records and audit history for 3 years. No external identity provider is required; no DR Region is provisioned.",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "availability_zone": "us-east-1a",
  "availability_zones": [
    "us-east-1a"
  ],
  "dr_region": "",
  "lz_version": 1,
  "lz_hash": "f9fff5e1fd38f60b",
  "requirements": [
    {
      "id": "REQ-01",
      "text": "The system shall allow employees to sign in using company email credentials with role-based access control.",
      "kind": "functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-02",
      "text": "The system shall allow employees to submit, view, and comment on maintenance requests with title, description, location, category, and priority.",
      "kind": "functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-03",
      "text": "The system shall generate a unique request ID for every submitted request and record timestamps and user identity for every status change.",
      "kind": "functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-04",
      "text": "The system shall allow maintenance staff to view all open requests, assign them to personnel, and update statuses through the workflow: Submitted, Assigned, In Progress, Resolved, Closed.",
      "kind": "functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-05",
      "text": "The system shall send an email notification within 60 seconds of a status change.",
      "kind": "functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-06",
      "text": "The system shall provide a dashboard showing request counts by status, category, and priority, and allow administrators to export filtered records as UTF-8 CSV files (up to 10,000 records).",
      "kind": "functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-07",
      "text": "The system shall allow administrators to create, disable, and reactivate user accounts.",
      "kind": "functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-08",
      "text": "The system shall support 525 registered users and 2,000 maintenance requests per month, with a growth path to 10,000 requests per month.",
      "kind": "non_functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-09",
      "text": "95% of request submission operations shall complete within 2 seconds under 50 concurrent users.",
      "kind": "non_functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-10",
      "text": "95% of dashboard queries shall complete within 3 seconds for a dataset of 100,000 requests.",
      "kind": "non_functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-11",
      "text": "The system shall target 99.0% monthly availability within a single-AZ deployment in us-east-1a.",
      "kind": "non_functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-12",
      "text": "The recovery point objective shall be 24 hours and the recovery time objective shall be 8 hours.",
      "kind": "non_functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-13",
      "text": "Request records, comments, and audit history shall be retained for 3 years; expired records shall be deleted within 30 days after the retention period ends.",
      "kind": "non_functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-14",
      "text": "All data in transit shall use TLS 1.2 or later and access shall enforce role-based authorization.",
      "kind": "non_functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-15",
      "text": "Total AWS infrastructure expenditure shall remain below USD 100 per month.",
      "kind": "constraint"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-16",
      "text": "All zonal resources must reside in us-east-1a; the application must use AWS-native managed services only; no third-party SaaS for core request processing.",
      "kind": "constraint"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-17",
      "text": "Application errors, failed notifications, and request-processing failures shall be logged and retained for 30 days.",
      "kind": "non_functional"
    },
    {
      "id": "REQ-18",
      "text": "A qualified engineer shall be able to deploy a routine application update within 30 minutes using documented procedures.",
      "kind": "non_functional"
    }
  ],
  "decisions": [
    {
      "id": "ADR-001",
      "title": "Use AWS Fargate (single task) for the application API and web serving",
      "status": "Accepted",
      "context": "The portal serves 525 users with at most 50 concurrent users (REQ-08, REQ-09). The SRS mandates a single-AZ deployment (REQ-11, REQ-16) and a USD 100/month cost ceiling (REQ-15). A long-running web/API service with persistent HTTP connections is needed. The deployment must be updatable within 30 minutes (REQ-18).",
      "decision": "Use one AWS Fargate task (Linux/ARM64, 0.5 vCPU / 1 GB) in the private-app subnet of us-east-1a. A single task is sufficient for the stated concurrency; the ECS service can scale to additional tasks if load grows. Container images are stored in Amazon ECR.",
      "consequences": [
        "Graviton ARM64 minimises compute cost, keeping the design within the USD 100 budget.",
        "A single task means no redundancy within the AZ; a task failure causes a brief outage until ECS restarts it (consistent with the 99.0% availability target).",
        "Scaling to 10,000 requests/month (REQ-08) is achieved by increasing the desired task count without workflow changes.",
        "Deployments via ECS rolling update satisfy the 30-minute update requirement (REQ-18)."
      ],
      "rejected_alternatives": [
        {
          "option": "AWS Lambda for the API",
          "reason": "Lambda cold starts and the 15-minute execution limit are unsuitable for a stateful web session and streaming CSV exports up to 10,000 rows (REQ-06); Lambda would also require API Gateway, adding cost."
        },
        {
          "option": "Amazon EC2 t4g.micro",
          "reason": "EC2 requires OS patching and AMI management, violating the managed-services constraint (REQ-16), and a t4g.micro has only 1 GiB RAM which is the same as the Fargate task but with higher operational overhead."
        }
      ],
      "requirement_ids": [
        "REQ-08",
        "REQ-09",
        "REQ-11",
        "REQ-15",
        "REQ-16",
        "REQ-18"
      ],
      "component_ids": [
        "C-03",
        "C-04"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "ADR-002",
      "title": "Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ for request and audit data",
      "status": "Accepted",
      "context": "The data model is relational: requests, assignments, comments, and audit events require joins and transactions (REQ-03, REQ-10). The dashboard must query 100,000 records within 3 seconds (REQ-10). The SRS mandates single-AZ deployment (REQ-16) and a 24-hour RPO / 8-hour RTO (REQ-12). The cost ceiling is USD 100/month (REQ-15).",
      "decision": "Use one Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 Single-AZ instance, db.t4g.micro, gp3 20 GiB, 7-day automated backups with point-in-time recovery, encrypted with the customer managed KMS key, placed in the private-data subnet of us-east-1a.",
      "consequences": [
        "Automated daily snapshots and PITR satisfy the 24-hour RPO; restoring a snapshot to a new instance satisfies the 8-hour RTO.",
        "Single-AZ means a hardware failure requires a snapshot restore, which is accepted per the 99.0% availability target and customer sign-off.",
        "db.t4g.micro (2 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM) is the smallest Graviton RDS size; move to db.t4g.small when average CPU exceeds 70% or free memory drops below 200 MiB.",
        "PostgreSQL full-text search and window functions satisfy the dashboard query requirement without a separate analytics service."
      ],
      "rejected_alternatives": [
        {
          "option": "Amazon DynamoDB",
          "reason": "Dashboard queries (REQ-10) require aggregations and joins across requests, assignments, and audit events that are natural in SQL but expensive to model in DynamoDB."
        },
        {
          "option": "Amazon Aurora Serverless v2",
          "reason": "Aurora's minimum cost (0.5 ACU minimum) exceeds the db.t4g.micro price and would push the design over the USD 100 budget (REQ-15)."
        }
      ],
      "requirement_ids": [
        "REQ-03",
        "REQ-10",
        "REQ-12",
        "REQ-13",
        "REQ-15",
        "REQ-16"
      ],
      "component_ids": [
        "C-07"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "ADR-003",
      "title": "Use Amazon Cognito for user authentication and RBAC",
      "status": "Accepted",
      "context": "The portal requires email-and-password sign-in for 525 users with three roles (employee, maintenance staff, administrator) and no external identity provider (REQ-01, REQ-07, REQ-14). The solution must use AWS-native managed services (REQ-16).",
      "decision": "Use one Amazon Cognito user pool (Essentials tier) with email-and-password authentication. Three Cognito groups map to the three application roles. The application validates the JWT issued by Cognito on every API request to enforce RBAC.",
      "consequences": [
        "Cognito's free tier (50,000 MAUs) covers the 525-user base at zero incremental cost, supporting the USD 100 budget.",
        "Administrators manage user accounts (create, disable, reactivate) via the Cognito admin API called from the application (REQ-07).",
        "Password reset and account recovery are handled natively by Cognito, reducing application code.",
        "If Northstar later requires SAML federation, Cognito supports it without replacing the authentication layer."
      ],
      "rejected_alternatives": [
        {
          "option": "Custom JWT authentication in the application",
          "reason": "Building and maintaining a secure credential store violates the managed-services constraint (REQ-16) and introduces security risk."
        }
      ],
      "requirement_ids": [
        "REQ-01",
        "REQ-07",
        "REQ-14",
        "REQ-16"
      ],
      "component_ids": [
        "C-06"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "ADR-004",
      "title": "Use Amazon SES for email status notifications",
      "status": "Accepted",
      "context": "The system must send email notifications within 60 seconds of a status change (REQ-05). The SRS requires an AWS-native service and no third-party SaaS (REQ-16). The customer provides a verified company email domain (Section 2.5).",
      "decision": "Use Amazon SES with one verified domain identity and DKIM enabled. The application API calls SES directly via the AWS SDK on each status-change event. SES delivery failures are logged to CloudWatch.",
      "consequences": [
        "SES sends email within seconds of the API call, satisfying the 60-second notification requirement.",
        "SES sandbox mode must be exited before go-live; the customer must verify the sending domain (OI-02).",
        "SES is a regional service with no VPC placement required; the Fargate task reaches it via the NAT Gateway.",
        "Bounces and complaints are handled via SES event notifications to CloudWatch."
      ],
      "rejected_alternatives": [
        {
          "option": "Amazon SNS email subscriptions",
          "reason": "SNS email is intended for operational alerts, not transactional application notifications; it does not support HTML templates or per-recipient personalisation needed for status notifications."
        }
      ],
      "requirement_ids": [
        "REQ-05",
        "REQ-16"
      ],
      "component_ids": [
        "C-09"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "ADR-005",
      "title": "Use Application Load Balancer with AWS WAF as the public entry point",
      "status": "Accepted",
      "context": "The platform contract mandates a per-workload WAF and a distributed ingress pattern with the ALB in the public tier (ingress: distributed, waf: per-workload). All browser communications must use HTTPS (REQ-14, C-03). The ALB terminates TLS and forwards to the Fargate task.",
      "decision": "Deploy one internet-facing Application Load Balancer (single_az in us-east-1a, the only AZ in this deployment) with an HTTPS 443 listener and an ACM certificate. Attach one AWS WAF web ACL (AWS managed Core Rule Set, Known Bad Inputs, and one rate-based rule) to the ALB.",
      "consequences": [
        "TLS termination at the ALB enforces HTTPS for all browser traffic (REQ-14).",
        "WAF protects against common web exploits and rate-based abuse without additional cost beyond the WAF ACL and rule charges.",
        "The ALB and WAF are the only components in the public subnet; all application and data resources remain private.",
        "ALB access logs provide an audit trail of all inbound requests."
      ],
      "rejected_alternatives": [
        {
          "option": "Amazon API Gateway HTTP API",
          "reason": "API Gateway adds per-request cost and is optimised for REST/HTTP APIs rather than serving a full web application with file downloads and session-based flows; ALB is more cost-effective at this scale."
        }
      ],
      "requirement_ids": [
        "REQ-14",
        "REQ-15",
        "REQ-16"
      ],
      "component_ids": [
        "C-01",
        "C-02"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "ADR-006",
      "title": "Use Amazon S3 for CSV exports and static assets with lifecycle retention",
      "status": "Accepted",
      "context": "Administrators export filtered request records as CSV files up to 10,000 rows (REQ-06). Request records and audit history must be retained for 3 years and deleted within 30 days after expiry (REQ-13). A cost-effective object store is needed (REQ-15).",
      "decision": "Use one Amazon S3 bucket for CSV exports and application static assets. Enable SSE-KMS encryption, versioning, and Block Public Access. Apply an S3 lifecycle rule to transition objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days and expire them after 3 years plus 30 days (1,125 days total).",
      "consequences": [
        "Lifecycle rules automate the 3-year retention and 30-day deletion window (REQ-13) without manual intervention.",
        "Pre-signed URLs generated by the API allow secure browser downloads without making the bucket public.",
        "S3 Standard storage cost for the expected export volume is negligible within the USD 100 budget.",
        "Glacier transition reduces long-term storage cost for aged exports."
      ],
      "rejected_alternatives": [
        {
          "option": "Serving CSV directly from the database via the API response stream",
          "reason": "Streaming large exports through the Fargate task ties up the task for the duration of the download and does not provide durable storage or audit of exported files."
        }
      ],
      "requirement_ids": [
        "REQ-06",
        "REQ-13",
        "REQ-15"
      ],
      "component_ids": [
        "C-08"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "ADR-007",
      "title": "Use AWS Backup for automated database snapshots to meet RPO/RTO",
      "status": "Accepted",
      "context": "The RPO is 24 hours and the RTO is 8 hours (REQ-12). The deployment is single-AZ with no DR Region (REQ-16, contract). The customer must approve the backup and recovery procedure (OI-03).",
      "decision": "Use AWS Backup with a daily backup plan targeting the RDS instance, a 7-day retention window in the primary vault, and a backup window of 02:00–03:00 UTC. RDS automated backups (7-day retention, PITR) are also enabled as a secondary recovery path.",
      "consequences": [
        "Daily snapshots satisfy the 24-hour RPO; restoring a snapshot to a new db.t4g.micro instance in us-east-1a satisfies the 8-hour RTO.",
        "AWS Backup provides centralised visibility and policy-driven compliance reporting for OI-03.",
        "Snapshot storage cost is minimal for a 20 GiB database.",
        "A hardware failure in the single AZ requires a restore; there is no automatic failover."
      ],
      "rejected_alternatives": [
        {
          "option": "RDS automated backups only (no AWS Backup)",
          "reason": "AWS Backup provides a centralised audit trail and policy enforcement required by the customer's information security policy (NFR-11); RDS automated backups alone do not satisfy the compliance reporting need."
        }
      ],
      "requirement_ids": [
        "REQ-12",
        "REQ-13",
        "REQ-15"
      ],
      "component_ids": [
        "C-07",
        "C-10"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "boundaries": [
    {
      "id": "acct_prod",
      "type": "account",
      "name": "northstar-maintenance-portal-prod",
      "parent": null,
      "cidr": "",
      "tier": "",
      "azs": [],
      "cidr_per_az": [],
      "account": "northstar-maintenance-portal-prod",
      "region": "",
      "prefilled": true
    },
    {
      "id": "region_prod",
      "type": "region",
      "name": "us-east-1 (primary)",
      "parent": "acct_prod",

  "security_operations": [
    "All inbound traffic enters exclusively through the Application Load Balancer (C-02) on port 443; the WAF (C-01) inspects every request before it reaches the Portal API (C-04). Security groups allow port 443 inbound only from 0.0.0.0/0 on the ALB; the Portal API security group allows port 8080 only from the ALB security group; the Request Database security group allows port 5432 only from the Portal API security group.",
    "All data at rest is encrypted: the Request Database (C-07) and Export and Assets Bucket (C-08) use the customer managed KMS key (C-11) via SSE-KMS. S3 Block Public Access is enabled on C-08.",
    "All data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or higher: HTTPS is enforced at the ALB (C-02); the Portal API (C-04) communicates with AWS services over TLS; the RDS connection uses SSL with certificate verification.",
    "The Portal API (C-04) runs under a least-privilege IAM role scoped to: read from Secrets Manager (C-12), send email via SES (C-09), read/write the S3 bucket (C-08), and write CloudWatch logs (C-13). No wildcard actions or resource ARNs are permitted.",
    "RDS master credentials are stored in Secrets Manager (C-12) with automatic rotation every 30 days. No long-lived access keys are used anywhere in the workload.",
    "Amazon Cognito (C-06) issues short-lived JWTs; the Portal API validates the token signature and group membership on every API call to enforce RBAC across employee, maintenance staff, and administrator roles.",
    "CloudWatch (C-13) retains all application and infrastructure logs for 30 days. Alarms are configured on application error rates, failed SES notifications, ECS task CPU and memory, and RDS CPU and free storage.",
    "AWS CloudTrail (provided by platform) records all API calls across the account. The S3 gateway endpoint (C-14) ensures S3 traffic does not traverse the public internet.",
    "The ECR repository (C-05) has scan-on-push enabled; critical vulnerabilities must be remediated before deploying a new image. The ECS task definition uses read-only root filesystem and drops all Linux capabilities not required by the application.",
    "AWS Backup (C-10) enforces a backup vault lock policy preventing deletion of snapshots within the 7-day retention window, supporting the RPO of 24 hours and the customer's information security policy."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    {
      "id": "ASM-01",
      "text": "The Portal API container listens on port 8080 and the ALB target group is configured accordingly.",
      "reason": "The SRS does not specify an application port; 8080 is the conventional non-privileged HTTP port for containerised web applications."
    },
    {
      "id": "ASM-02",
      "text": "MFA is optional (not enforced) in the Cognito user pool.",
      "reason": "The SRS requires email-and-password authentication (Section 5) but does not mandate MFA; optional MFA allows administrators to enable it later without a design change."
    },
    {
      "id": "ASM-03",
      "text": "The RDS instance uses db.t4g.micro (2 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM), the smallest Graviton RDS size.",
      "reason": "The SRS data volumes (525 users, 100,000 requests over the operating period) are modest; db.t4g.micro is the most cost-effective choice to stay within the USD 100/month budget (REQ-15). Upgrade to db.t4g.small when average CPU exceeds 70% or free memory drops below 200 MiB."
    },
    {
      "id": "ASM-04",
      "text": "The Fargate task uses 0.5 vCPU and 1 GB memory, the smallest valid Fargate configuration.",
      "reason": "50 concurrent users (REQ-09) with a stateless API is well within the capacity of a single small Fargate task; this minimises cost (REQ-15)."
    },
    {
      "id": "ASM-05",
      "text": "SES is used in the us-east-1 region and the customer will exit SES sandbox mode before go-live.",
      "reason": "SES sandbox mode restricts sending to verified addresses only; production use requires sandbox exit, which depends on the customer verifying their domain (OI-02)."
    },
    {
      "id": "ASM-06",
      "text": "The S3 lifecycle expiration is set to 1,125 days (3 years × 365 days + 30 days grace period) to satisfy the retention and deletion requirements.",
      "reason": "REQ-13 requires 3-year retention and deletion within 30 days after expiry; 1,125 days covers both without manual intervention."
    },
    {
      "id": "ASM-07",
      "text": "The ACM certificate for the ALB is issued for the customer's domain and managed by ACM for automatic renewal.",
      "reason": "The SRS requires HTTPS (C-03) but does not specify the domain name; ACM-managed certificates eliminate manual renewal overhead."
    },
    {
      "id": "ASM-08",
      "text": "No ElastiCache or query caching layer is added for dashboard queries.",
      "reason": "PostgreSQL with appropriate indexes on a db.t4g.micro can satisfy the 3-second dashboard query target (REQ-10) for 100,000 records; a cache would add cost that risks breaching the USD 100 budget (REQ-15)."
    }
  ],
