| Deployment | One Region (us-east-1), 1 Availability Zone (us-east-1a) |
| DR Region | None |
| Usage entries | 13 |
| Warnings | 4 |

## 1. Warnings

- C-10 (AWS Backup): AWS Backup is not in the tool schema and has been omitted from the usage file. It manages daily RDS snapshots with 7-day retention; the backup storage cost is driven by the RDS instance size (~20 GB per snapshot × 7 snapshots = ~140 GB of backup storage).
- C-14 (VPC Endpoints / AWS PrivateLink): The design configures only an S3 gateway endpoint, which is free. The endpoint_count is set to 0 and no cost will be incurred. If interface endpoints are added later (e.g., for ECR, Secrets Manager, or CloudWatch), costs will increase.
- NFR-10 / C-05 (Cost constraint): The $100/month budget is tight. The always-on Fargate task, RDS db.t4g.micro, NAT Gateway, and CloudWatch log ingestion together likely approach or exceed $100/month; the customer should validate the cost estimate carefully before deployment.
- C-08 (S3 Glacier): Objects transitioned to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days are not counted in the Standard storage figure. Over 3 years, accumulated Glacier storage could reach several GB; retrieval costs apply if exports are accessed after transition.

## 2. Workload profile

Every usage figure below is derived from these drivers. Basis: stated (in the SRS), inferred (calculated from stated numbers) or assumed (the SRS is silent).

| Driver | Value | Basis | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registered users | 525 users | stated | NFR-01: 'The system shall support 525 registered users and 2,000 maintenance requests per month.' |
| Monthly active users | 400 users | assumed | Not all 525 registered users will be active every month; ~76% MAU rate is typical for an internal business tool. Employees (500) likely check status occasionally; maintenance staff (20) and admins (5) are daily users. |
| Maintenance requests per month | 2000 requests/month | stated | NFR-01: '2,000 maintenance requests per month'. |
| Status changes per request | 3 status changes/request | assumed | FR-07 defines 5 statuses (Submitted → Assigned → In Progress → Resolved → Closed). A typical request transitions through ~3 changes on average (not all reach every state). |
| Status change events per month | 6000 events/month | inferred | 2,000 requests × 3 status changes = 6,000 status change events per month. |
| Email notifications per month | 6000 emails/month | inferred | FR-09 requires one email per status change; 6,000 status changes = 6,000 emails per month. |
| HTTP API requests per month (ALB/WAF) | 300000 requests/month | assumed | 400 MAU × ~25 sessions/month × ~30 HTTP requests/session = 300,000 requests/month. Sessions include browsing, submitting, and checking requests; 30 requests/session covers page loads, API calls, and asset fetches. |
| Average request payload size | 5 KB | assumed | Typical REST API payload for a maintenance request form or list response; small JSON objects. |
| Database storage | 5 GB | inferred | 100,000 requests × ~5 KB average record (request + assignments + comments + audit) = ~500 MB over 3 years; well within the 20 GB allocated. Steady-state monthly growth is small. |
| CSV exports per month | 10 exports/month | assumed | 5 administrators; assume ~2 exports per admin per month on average for reporting purposes. |
| Average CSV export size | 1 MB | assumed | Up to 10,000 records at ~100 bytes/record = ~1 MB per export file. |
| Application log volume per month | 2 GB/month | assumed | 300,000 requests × ~1 KB log line per request ≈ 300 MB for access logs; ECS task logs, RDS logs, and error traces add ~1.7 GB; total ~2 GB/month is typical for a low-traffic internal app. |
| Container image size | 0.5 GB | assumed | A typical Node.js or Python REST API container image is 200–500 MB; 10 images retained by lifecycle policy = ~5 GB stored in ECR. |

## 3. Usage by component

| Component | Service | Usage figures | How the figures were reached | Assumed fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-01 Web Application Firewall | AWS WAF | web_acl_count: 1; rules_per_acl: 3; requests_inspected_per_month: 300,000; managed_rule_groups: 2 | 1 web ACL with 2 managed rule groups (AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet and AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet) plus 1 rate-based rule = 3 rules per ACL. WAF inspects all requests reaching the ALB: 400 MAU × 25 sessions × 30 requests = 300,000 requests/month. | requests_inspected_per_month |
| C-03 NAT Gateway | NAT Gateway | gateway_count: 1; data_processed_gb: 1.5; availability_zones: 1 | 1 NAT Gateway in us-east-1a. Outbound traffic is primarily SES API calls (6,000 emails × ~5 KB = ~30 MB) and ECR image pulls (~0.5 GB/deploy, ~2 deploys/month = ~1 GB); S3 traffic is routed via the gateway endpoint and does not pass through NAT. Total ~1.5 GB/month. | data_processed_gb |
| C-14 VPC Endpoints | AWS PrivateLink | endpoint_count: 0; data_processed_gb: 0; endpoint_type: Gateway | The design configures only an S3 gateway endpoint (no additional interface endpoints). S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints are free and do not count as billable PrivateLink interface endpoints. There are no interface endpoints in this design. | none |
| C-02 Application Load Balancer | Application Load Balancer | load_balancer_count: 1; lcu_per_hour: 0.5; rules_count: 2; availability_zones: 1 | Single internet-facing ALB in us-east-1a. At 300,000 requests/month (~7 req/s average) with small payloads (~5 KB), LCU consumption is well below 1 LCU/hour; 0.5 LCU/hour is a conservative estimate. 2 listener rules covers the HTTPS:443 default rule plus one path-based rule. | lcu_per_hour, rules_count |
| C-04 Portal API | AWS Fargate | vcpu_hours_per_month: 365; memory_gb_per_month: 730; operating_system: Linux; architecture: arm64 | 1 always-on task at 0.5 vCPU and 1 GB memory × 730 hours/month = 365 vCPU-hours and 730 GB-hours per month. The design specifies Linux/ARM64 with desired_tasks = 1. | none |
| C-05 Container Registry | Amazon ECR | storage_gb: 5; data_transfer_out_gb: 0; repositories: 1; image_scans_per_month: 2 | Lifecycle policy keeps last 10 images; at ~0.5 GB per image = 5 GB stored. Fargate pulls images within the same Region so data transfer out is 0 GB. Assuming ~2 image pushes (deployments) per month triggers 2 scan-on-push scans. | storage_gb, image_scans_per_month |
| C-07 Request Database | Amazon RDS | engine: PostgreSQL; instance_class: db.t4g.micro; instance_count: 1; storage_gb: 20; multi_az: false; backup_retention_days: 7 | Single-AZ db.t4g.micro PostgreSQL 17 instance with 20 GB gp3 storage as specified in the design. Multi-AZ is explicitly false per the design and the single-AZ deployment constraint. 7-day automated backup retention is set in the configuration. | none |
| C-08 Export and Assets Bucket | Amazon S3 | storage_class: Standard; storage_gb: 0.5; get_requests_per_month: 15,000; put_requests_per_month: 1,500; data_transfer_out_gb: 0.1 | Active S3 Standard storage holds recent CSV exports (10 exports × 1 MB = 10 MB) and static assets (~490 MB); objects older than 90 days transition to Glacier. GET requests: 300,000 page loads × ~5% hitting S3 assets = 15,000 GETs/month. PUT requests: 10 CSV exports + ~1,490 static asset deploys/updates = ~1,500 PUTs/month. Pre-signed URL downloads by admins are small (~10 × 1 MB = 10 MB); data transfer out to internet is minimal. | storage_gb, get_requests_per_month, put_requests_per_month, data_transfer_out_gb |
| C-09 Email Notification Service | Amazon SES | emails_per_month: 6,000; attachments_gb: 0; dedicated_ip: false; region: us-east-1 | 6,000 status-change events per month (2,000 requests × 3 average status changes) each trigger one email notification per FR-09. Emails are plain-text or HTML with no attachments. Shared IP pool is used per the design configuration. | none |
| C-06 User Pool | Amazon Cognito | monthly_active_users: 400; user_pool_count: 1; advanced_security: false; mfa_enabled: false | 1 user pool (Essentials tier) for 525 registered users; ~400 MAU estimated (76% of registered users active in a given month). MFA is optional per ASM-02 and the design configuration, so it is not enforced. Essentials tier does not include advanced security features. | monthly_active_users |
| C-12 Secrets Store | AWS Secrets Manager | secrets_count: 1; api_calls_per_month: 60; rotation_enabled: true; rotation_frequency_days: 30 | 1 secret for RDS master credentials with 30-day rotation. The Fargate task retrieves the secret at startup and caches it; with 1 always-on task and occasional restarts, ~2 GetSecretValue calls/day × 30 days = 60 API calls/month. | api_calls_per_month |
| C-11 Encryption Key | AWS KMS | customer_managed_keys: 1; api_calls_per_month: 15,000; key_type: Symmetric; multi_region: false | 1 symmetric CMK used for RDS SSE and S3 SSE-KMS. RDS generates ~1 data key per connection; at ~100 connections/day × 30 days = 3,000 calls. S3 Bucket Key reduces per-object KMS calls; ~1,500 PUT requests generate ~1,500 KMS calls; GET requests use cached data keys. CloudWatch and Secrets Manager add ~500 calls. Total ~5,000–15,000 calls/month; 15,000 is a conservative upper estimate. | api_calls_per_month |
| C-13 Observability | Amazon CloudWatch | metrics_per_month: 6; logs_ingested_gb_per_month: 2; log_storage_gb: 2; alarms_count: 6; dashboards_count: 1 | 6 custom alarms (errors, failed_notifications, task_cpu, task_memory, rds_cpu, rds_free_storage) and 1 operational dashboard. Log ingestion: ~2 GB/month across portal-api, ecs-task, and rds-postgresql log groups. With 30-day retention, steady-state log storage is ~2 GB (one month's worth). 6 custom metrics corresponding to the alarm dimensions. | metrics_per_month, logs_ingested_gb_per_month, log_storage_gb |

## 4. Notes

- This is a low-traffic internal portal: 525 users, 2,000 requests/month, and a single always-on Fargate task with a single-AZ RDS micro instance. The workload is very small by AWS standards.
- The dominant cost drivers are the NAT Gateway (hourly charge plus data processing), the always-on Fargate task (730 hours/month at 0.5 vCPU / 1 GB), and the RDS db.t4g.micro instance (730 hours/month). CloudWatch log ingestion (~2 GB/month) and the KMS CMK add modest but non-trivial costs.
- SES email volume (6,000/month) and S3 usage are negligible in cost terms. Cognito at 400 MAU on the Essentials tier is also low cost.
- The estimate would change most if: (1) the NAT Gateway data volume increases significantly (e.g., if ECR pulls are frequent or SES traffic grows), (2) the Fargate task is scaled out, or (3) CloudWatch log retention or volume increases. The $100/month budget constraint (REQ-15/NFR-10) should be validated against the priced output.

## 5. Method

- Configuration fields (instance class, engine, memory, storage size, counts) are copied from the ADR design; usage fields are estimated from the workload profile by one model call.
- One expected steady-state month of 730 hours. Prices, free tier and cost are left to the cost calculator.
- multi_az and availability_zones follow the design: the component's deployment configuration, its placement and AZs, and the design's Availability Zones. The estimate adds no standby, replica or AZ the design does not state. memory_gb is computed from memory_mb.
- Shared platform services (Transit Gateway, central inspection and egress, hub VPCs, the security and logging accounts) are not priced; the estimate covers this workload only.
- Components added later by the diagram's Assumer are not included; usage.json covers the ADR design only.

wa_review.md.data:
# Well-Architected review: Equipment Maintenance Request Portal

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Design version | 1 |
| Review round | 1 |
| Compared with | First review |
| Framework | AWS Well-Architected Framework, doc revision November 6, 2024 (snapshot 2026-10-27) |
| Overall score | 75% |
| Open findings | 61 (4 high, 30 medium, 27 low) |
| Generated | 2026-10-30T08:12:19.623282+00:00 |
| Model | us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 |

## 1. Summary by pillar

| Pillar | Score | High | Medium | Low | Met | Partial | Not met | N/A | Constraint | Accepted risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operational excellence | 45% | 2 | 5 | 2 | 2 | 6 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Security | 84% | 0 | 4 | 6 | 25 | 9 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| Reliability | 68% | 2 | 13 | 8 | 22 | 17 | 6 | 6 | 0 | 0 |
| Performance efficiency | 92% | 0 | 1 | 2 | 15 | 3 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| Cost optimization | 65% | 0 | 7 | 5 | 8 | 10 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Sustainability | 89% | 0 | 0 | 4 | 14 | 4 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 0 |

- **Operational excellence:** The design establishes a solid operational foundation with CloudWatch logging, alarms, and a dashboard covering infrastructure metrics and error rates. The most important gap is the absence of business KPIs, distributed tracing (X-Ray), user experience monitoring (RUM/synthetics), and automated alarm responses, leaving the team reliant on manual intervention and user-reported issues.
- **Security:** Security is well-addressed: network layering, WAF, least-privilege IAM, KMS encryption at rest, TLS in transit, Secrets Manager rotation, and platform-provided GuardDuty/Security Hub are all in place. The most important gaps are optional MFA for privileged roles, the absence of an emergency access process, no container image signing, and no automated remediation for non-compliant resources.
- **Reliability:** The single-AZ deployment is an accepted customer constraint, and the backup/restore strategy meets the stated 24-hour RPO and 8-hour RTO on paper. The most critical gaps are the absence of defined retry/timeout/backoff policies, no ECS auto-scaling policy, no emergency levers, no distributed tracing for root-cause analysis, and an untested, non-automated DR restore runbook.
- **Performance efficiency:** Compute and data store selections are well-reasoned for the workload size, using Graviton instances and purpose-built managed services. The key gaps are the absence of a defined ECS auto-scaling policy to handle growth to 10,000 requests/month, unspecified database indexes for the dashboard query SLA, and no validation of the dashboard query performance assumption on db.t4g.micro.
- **Cost optimization:** The design makes cost-conscious choices (Graviton, Fargate, free-tier Cognito, S3 lifecycle) and stays within the USD 100 constraint in intent, but lacks a formal Pricing Calculator estimate, resource tagging, Savings Plans/Reserved Instance commitments for permanently running resources, and a cost projection for the growth scenario.
- **Sustainability:** The design uses managed services, Graviton ARM64 instances, and S3 lifecycle policies, which are strong sustainability choices. The main gaps are the absence of ECS auto-scaling (preventing scale-to-zero during off-hours) and synchronous notification dispatch that creates unnecessary peak load rather than using buffered, asynchronous processing.

## 2. Findings


### High risk

| Best practice | Pillar | Status | Scope | Finding | Recommendation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OPS04-BP03 Implement user experience telemetry | Operational excellence | not met | Workload | The design has no real user monitoring (RUM) or synthetic transaction capability; user-facing performance issues (e.g., slow page loads, failed submissions) would only be detected through user reports or backend error logs. | Add Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canaries to simulate login, request submission, and dashboard load flows, providing proactive detection of user-facing availability and performance degradations. | C-02, C-13, REQ-09 |
| OPS04-BP05 Implement distributed tracing | Operational excellence | not met | Workload | The design does not include distributed tracing; there is no AWS X-Ray or equivalent instrumentation described for the Portal API (C-04) or its calls to RDS (C-07), SES (C-09), Cognito (C-06), or S3 (C-08). | Enable AWS X-Ray tracing on the ECS task definition for C-04 and instrument the application SDK calls to RDS, SES, Cognito, and S3 to provide end-to-end request tracing. | C-04, C-13 |
| REL05-BP03 Control and limit retry calls | Reliability | not met | Workload | The design does not describe retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter for the Portal API's (C-04) calls to RDS (C-07), SES (C-09), Secrets Manager (C-12), or S3 (C-08); AWS SDK defaults may not be appropriate for this workload. | Explicitly configure AWS SDK retry settings in the Portal API (C-04) with exponential backoff, jitter, and a maximum retry count for each downstream dependency (RDS, SES, S3, Secrets Manager), and document these values in the application configuration. | C-04, C-07, C-09 |
| REL05-BP05 Set client timeouts | Reliability | not met | Workload | The design does not specify connection timeout or statement timeout values for the Portal API's (C-04) connections to RDS (C-07) or for SDK call timeouts to SES (C-09) and Secrets Manager (C-12). | Define explicit connection timeouts (e.g., 5 s connect, 30 s statement for RDS) and SDK call timeouts (e.g., 3 s for SES, 2 s for Secrets Manager) in the Portal API (C-04) configuration to prevent hung requests from exhausting the single Fargate task. | C-04, C-07, C-09 |

### Medium risk

| Best practice | Pillar | Status | Scope | Finding | Recommendation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| COST03-BP02 Add organization information to cost and usage | Cost optimization | not met | Workload | The design does not define a resource tagging schema; no cost allocation tags are applied to the ALB, Fargate task, RDS instance, S3 bucket, or KMS key to enable cost attribution and filtering in AWS Cost Explorer. | Define a mandatory tagging schema (e.g., Project=maintenance-portal, Environment=prod, Owner=northstar-ops) and apply it to all resources in the design, enforced via an SCP or AWS Config tag-compliance rule. | C-04, C-07, C-08, REQ-15 |
| COST03-BP03 Identify cost attribution categories | Cost optimization | partial | Workload | The design targets a USD 100/month budget (REQ-15) but does not identify cost attribution categories (e.g., compute, storage, networking, security) or assign ownership to enable spend accountability. | Define cost attribution categories in the design (compute: Fargate+RDS, storage: S3+backups, networking: ALB+NAT, security: WAF+KMS+Secrets Manager) and configure AWS Cost Explorer with these tag-based groupings. | REQ-15, REQ-10 |
| COST05-BP03 Perform a thorough analysis of each component | Cost optimization | partial | Workload | The design selects components but does not calculate the total cost of ownership including operational overhead (e.g., WAF ACL charges at ~$5/month, NAT Gateway hourly charges, KMS API call costs) to confirm the USD 100/month ceiling is met. | Produce an AWS Pricing Calculator estimate covering all components (ALB, WAF, Fargate, RDS, NAT Gateway, S3, SES, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, ECR, Backup) and include it in the design to validate REQ-15. | C-03, C-01, REQ-15 |
| COST06-BP01 Perform cost modeling | Cost optimization | partial | Workload | The design makes component selections with cost rationale (ADR-001, ADR-002) but does not include a formal cost model or benchmark comparing actual estimated monthly spend against the USD 100 ceiling across all components. | Create an AWS Pricing Calculator estimate for the baseline workload and include the monthly total in the design document, with a breakdown by component, to formally validate the USD 100 budget constraint (REQ-15). | REQ-15, C-03, C-01 |
| COST07-BP01 Perform pricing model analysis | Cost optimization | partial | Workload | The design uses on-demand pricing for Fargate and RDS without analyzing whether Compute Savings Plans or RDS Reserved Instances would reduce cost for these continuously running resources. | After 30 days of production operation, analyze Fargate and RDS usage patterns and purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan for Fargate and a 1-year RDS Reserved Instance for db.t4g.micro to reduce steady-state costs. | C-04, C-07, REQ-15 |
| COST08-BP01 Perform data transfer modeling | Cost optimization | partial | Workload | The design does not include a data transfer cost model; NAT Gateway data processing charges for SES API calls, Cognito token validation, and Secrets Manager reads from the Fargate task could be material within the USD 100 budget. | Add VPC interface endpoints for Secrets Manager (C-12) and Cognito (C-06) to eliminate NAT Gateway data processing charges for those high-frequency call paths, and include a data transfer cost estimate in the design. | C-03, C-08, C-09, REQ-15 |
| COST09-BP01 Perform an analysis on the workload demand | Cost optimization | partial | Workload | The design does not include a demand analysis covering peak usage patterns (e.g., Monday morning submission spikes, end-of-month reporting) that would inform scaling thresholds and reserved capacity decisions. | Document expected demand patterns (daily and weekly request submission peaks) in the design and use these to set ECS auto-scaling thresholds and to validate that the db.t4g.micro can handle peak query load. | REQ-08, REQ-09, REQ-15 |
| OPS04-BP01 Identify key performance indicators | Operational excellence | partial | Workload | CloudWatch (C-13) defines technical alarms on errors, CPU, and memory, but no business-level KPIs (e.g., request submission rate, notification delivery rate, mean time to resolution) are defined or tracked. | Add CloudWatch custom metrics and alarms for business KPIs—request submission rate, status-change notification success rate, and mean resolution time—emitted by the Portal API (C-04) to align observability with business outcomes. | C-13, REQ-17 |
| OPS04-BP02 Implement application telemetry | Operational excellence | partial | Workload | The design logs application errors and emits ECS/RDS infrastructure metrics, but does not describe structured application-level telemetry such as request lifecycle events, assignment durations, or notification latency emitted by the Portal API (C-04). | Instrument the Portal API (C-04) to emit structured log events and custom CloudWatch metrics for each request lifecycle transition, notification dispatch latency, and CSV export duration to provide actionable application-layer telemetry. | C-04, C-13, REQ-17 |
| OPS04-BP04 Implement dependency telemetry | Operational excellence | partial | Workload | SES delivery failures are logged to CloudWatch (ADR-004), but there is no monitoring of the RDS dependency health (connection pool exhaustion, replication lag) or Cognito token validation latency as external dependencies of the Portal API (C-04). | Add CloudWatch alarms on RDS DatabaseConnections and Cognito service health events, and configure SES event destination metrics for bounce and complaint rates, to provide complete dependency telemetry. | C-09, C-13, REQ-05 |
| OPS08-BP03 Analyze workload traces | Operational excellence | not met | Workload | The design specifies no distributed tracing (no X-Ray), so trace analysis to identify latency bottlenecks across the Portal API (C-04), RDS (C-07), and SES (C-09) call chain is not possible. | Enable AWS X-Ray on C-04 and configure the CloudWatch console ServiceLens view to correlate traces with logs and metrics for root-cause analysis. | C-13 |
| OPS08-BP04 Create actionable alerts | Operational excellence | partial | Workload | Alarms are defined on infrastructure metrics (CPU, memory, free storage) and error rates, but no alarm is defined for the business-critical 60-second notification SLA (REQ-05) or for request queue depth (e.g., requests stuck in Submitted status beyond a threshold). | Add a CloudWatch alarm on the SES notification latency custom metric and a separate alarm on the count of requests remaining in Submitted status beyond a configurable threshold to make KPI-at-risk conditions actionable. | C-13, REQ-17 |
| PERF02-BP05 Scale your compute resources dynamically | Performance efficiency | partial | Workload | The design states the ECS service can scale to additional tasks for the 10,000 requests/month growth path (ADR-001) but does not define a scaling policy, leaving dynamic scaling as an intention rather than a configured capability. | Define an ECS Application Auto Scaling target-tracking policy on ALB RequestCountPerTarget for the Portal API service (C-04) with documented scale-out and scale-in thresholds. | C-04, ADR-001, REQ-08 |
| REL01-BP01 Aware of service quotas and constraints | Reliability | partial | Workload | The design selects services and sizes but does not document awareness of relevant service quotas (e.g., Fargate task vCPU per account, RDS instance count, Cognito user pool MAU limits, SES sending rate) that could constrain the workload. | Add a service quota review section to the design documenting the default and required quotas for Fargate, RDS, Cognito, and SES in us-east-1, and confirm that current account quotas are sufficient for the 10,000 requests/month growth target (REQ-08). | C-04, C-07, C-06, REQ-08 |
| REL01-BP05 Automate quota management | Reliability | not met | Workload | The design does not describe any automated quota management process; quota increases required for the growth path to 10,000 requests/month (REQ-08) would need to be identified and requested manually. | Define an IaC-driven quota request process (e.g., using the AWS Service Quotas API in the deployment pipeline) that automatically requests increases for Fargate task count and SES sending rate when the workload is provisioned. | REQ-08, REQ-15 |
| REL05-BP01 Implement graceful degradation to transform applicable hard dependencies into soft dependencies | Reliability | partial | Workload | The Portal API (C-04) calls SES synchronously on every status change; if SES is temporarily unavailable, the design does not describe a degraded mode where the status change is still persisted and the notification is retried asynchronously. | Decouple notification dispatch from the status-change write path by persisting a pending notification record in RDS (C-07) and retrying SES delivery asynchronously (e.g., via a short-polling ECS task or EventBridge Scheduler), so a SES outage does not fail the status-change operation. | C-04, C-09, REQ-05 |
| REL05-BP02 Throttle requests | Reliability | partial | Workload | The WAF rate-based rule (C-01) provides coarse rate limiting at the perimeter, but the Portal API (C-04) has no application-level throttling on individual user or role-based request rates, leaving it vulnerable to a single authenticated user exhausting backend resources. | Implement per-user rate limiting in the Portal API (C-04) using an in-memory token bucket or a DynamoDB-backed counter, with HTTP 429 responses and Retry-After headers, to protect the RDS instance from individual user abuse. | C-02, C-01, REQ-09 |
| REL05-BP04 Fail fast and limit queues | Reliability | partial | Workload | The design does not describe a dead-letter or retry queue for failed SES notifications; a failed notification call is logged (ADR-004) but there is no mechanism to detect accumulation of undelivered notifications or to bound the retry window. | Persist failed SES notification attempts to a dedicated table in RDS (C-07) with a retry counter and last-attempt timestamp, add a CloudWatch alarm on the count of pending retries exceeding a threshold, and bound retries to a maximum of 3 attempts within 5 minutes. | C-04, C-09, REQ-05 |
| REL05-BP07 Implement emergency levers | Reliability | not met | Workload | The design has no emergency levers defined; there is no documented mechanism to disable email notifications, put the portal in read-only mode, or shed non-critical load during a partial failure of SES or RDS. | Implement feature flags stored in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store that the Portal API (C-04) reads at startup to enable read-only mode or disable notification dispatch, allowing operators to activate these levers without a redeployment. | C-04, C-09, REQ-05 |
| REL06-BP07 Monitor end-to-end tracing of requests through your system | Reliability | not met | Workload | The design does not include distributed tracing (no X-Ray), so end-to-end request tracing across the ALB (C-02), Portal API (C-04), RDS (C-07), and SES (C-09) is not available for debugging latency or failure root causes. | Enable AWS X-Ray active tracing on the ECS task definition for C-04 and configure the X-Ray daemon as a sidecar container, then use CloudWatch ServiceLens to correlate traces with logs and metrics. | C-04, C-13 |
| REL09-BP01 Identify and back up all data that needs to be backed up, or reproduce the data from sources | Reliability | partial | Workload | AWS Backup (C-10) and RDS automated backups cover the RDS instance (C-07), but the S3 bucket (C-08) containing CSV exports and static assets has versioning enabled but no explicit backup or cross-account copy policy to protect against accidental deletion. | Add an S3 Replication rule or AWS Backup plan targeting the Export and Assets Bucket (C-08) to create a recoverable copy of export files, ensuring all data sources are covered by the backup strategy. | C-08, C-10, REQ-13 |
| REL10-BP01 Deploy the workload to multiple locations | Reliability | partial | Platform | The workload is deployed in a single AZ (us-east-1a) by explicit customer choice, meaning an AZ failure causes a full outage; this is accepted per the SRS but is a gap against the best practice of multi-location deployment. | Document in the design that multi-AZ deployment is explicitly out of scope per the SRS (Section 2.3) and revisit this decision at the next contract renewal if the 99.0% availability target proves insufficient. | C-04, C-07, C-02, REQ-11 |
| REL11-BP02 Fail over to healthy resources | Reliability | partial | Workload | The ECS service restarts a failed Fargate task automatically, but there is no failover path for the RDS instance (C-07) in a single-AZ deployment; a database failure requires a manual snapshot restore with up to 8-hour RTO. | Document the RDS failure runbook explicitly, including the CloudWatch alarm that triggers the restore procedure and the step-by-step process to update the Secrets Manager endpoint (C-12) to point to the restored instance. | C-04, C-07, REQ-11 |
| REL11-BP03 Automate healing on all layers | Reliability | partial | Workload | ECS restarts a failed task automatically, but there is no auto-scaling policy defined, so the service cannot automatically add tasks in response to sustained high load or partial task failure, leaving the single task as a potential bottleneck. | Define an ECS Application Auto Scaling policy (minimum 1, maximum 3 tasks) with a target-tracking policy on CPU utilization or ALB request count to enable automated healing under load. | C-04, C-13 |
| REL13-BP02 Use defined recovery strategies to meet the recovery objectives | Reliability | partial | Workload | The DR strategy is backup-and-restore (snapshot restore to a new RDS instance), which is documented in ADR-007, but the strategy has not been tested and there is no documented runbook or automation to execute the restore within the 8-hour RTO. | Conduct a documented DR restore exercise against the RDS snapshot, record the actual restore time, and automate the restore steps using an AWS Systems Manager Automation document to ensure the 8-hour RTO is achievable. | ADR-007, C-10, REQ-12 |
| REL13-BP05 Automate recovery | Reliability | not met | Workload | The design relies entirely on manual snapshot restore for disaster recovery; there is no automated recovery workflow (e.g., EventBridge + Step Functions) to detect an RDS failure and initiate the restore process. | Implement an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook triggered by a CloudWatch alarm on RDS instance status that automatically initiates a snapshot restore to a new db.t4g.micro instance and updates the Secrets Manager endpoint, reducing manual steps in the recovery path. | ADR-007, C-10, REQ-12 |
| SEC02-BP01 Use strong sign-in mechanisms | Security | partial | Workload | MFA is configured as optional (ASM-02) in the Cognito user pool (C-06), meaning administrator and maintenance staff accounts can authenticate with password alone, increasing the risk of credential compromise. | Enforce MFA for the administrator and maintenance_staff Cognito groups in C-06 using Cognito's group-level MFA override, leaving it optional only for the employee group. | C-06, ASM-02, REQ-01 |
| SEC02-BP04 Rely on a centralized identity provider | Security | partial | Workload | Cognito is used as a standalone user directory with email/password credentials rather than federating to a centralized corporate identity provider; workforce users have a separate credential set for this portal. | Document in ADR-003 that SAML/OIDC federation to Northstar's corporate identity provider should be implemented when one becomes available, and add an open question to confirm whether Northstar has an existing IdP that should be integrated now. | C-06, ADR-003 |
| SEC03-BP03 Establish emergency access process | Security | not met | Workload | The design has no documented emergency access process for the portal if Cognito is unavailable or an administrator account is locked out, leaving no break-glass path to manage users or access the system. | Define an emergency access runbook that uses a pre-created, separately stored Cognito administrator account (or a direct RDS read-only credential in Secrets Manager) that can be activated without relying on the normal Cognito sign-in flow. | C-06, ADR-003 |
| SEC06-BP01 Perform vulnerability management | Security | partial | Workload | ECR scan-on-push is enabled for container images (C-05), but the design does not describe a vulnerability management process for the OS packages and application dependencies inside the Fargate task (C-04) between image rebuilds. | Enable Amazon Inspector for ECR continuous scanning on the C-05 repository so that newly discovered CVEs in existing images trigger alerts without requiring a new push, and define a remediation SLA for critical findings. | C-05, C-04 |

### Low risk

| Best practice | Pillar | Status | Scope | Finding | Recommendation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| COST05-BP06 Perform cost analysis for different usage over time | Cost optimization | partial | Workload | The design sizes components for current load (525 users, 2,000 requests/month) but does not analyze how costs evolve at the 10,000 requests/month growth target (REQ-08), where NAT Gateway data processing and RDS storage costs may increase significantly. | Add a cost projection for the 10,000 requests/month scenario to the design, specifically modeling NAT Gateway data processing charges, RDS storage growth, and SES per-email costs to confirm the USD 100 budget remains viable at scale. | C-04, C-07, REQ-08, REQ-15 |
| COST06-BP03 Select resource type, size, and number automatically based on metrics | Cost optimization | partial | Workload | The design does not describe using AWS Compute Optimizer or RDS Performance Insights to right-size the Fargate task and RDS instance based on actual runtime metrics after go-live. | Enable AWS Compute Optimizer for the ECS service and RDS Performance Insights for C-07, and schedule a right-sizing review 30 days after go-live to adjust Fargate vCPU/memory and RDS instance class based on observed utilization. | C-04, C-07 |
| COST07-BP04 Implement pricing models for all components of this workload | Cost optimization | not met | Workload | The Fargate task and RDS instance run continuously on on-demand pricing; no Savings Plans or Reserved Instances are specified for these permanently running resources. | Commit to a 1-year Compute Savings Plan for the Fargate task (C-04) and a 1-year Reserved Instance for the RDS db.t4g.micro (C-07) to reduce steady-state compute costs by approximately 30–40%. | C-04, C-07, REQ-15 |
| COST09-BP02 Implement a buffer or throttle to manage demand | Cost optimization | partial | Workload | The WAF rate-based rule (C-01) provides perimeter throttling but the Portal API (C-04) has no application-level buffering or throttling to smooth demand spikes and protect the RDS instance from burst query load. | Implement application-level request queuing or throttling in the Portal API (C-04) for bulk operations (CSV export, dashboard refresh) to flatten demand on the RDS instance and avoid over-provisioning for peak load. | C-02, C-01, C-04 |
| COST09-BP03 Supply resources dynamically | Cost optimization | partial | Workload | The ECS service is configured with a fixed desired count of 1 task and no auto-scaling policy, meaning resources are not dynamically supplied in response to demand changes. | Configure ECS Application Auto Scaling with a target-tracking policy so that compute resources are provisioned dynamically in response to actual demand, avoiding both over-provisioning at low load and under-provisioning at peak. | C-04, ADR-001, REQ-08 |
| OPS08-BP01 Analyze workload metrics | Operational excellence | partial | Workload | The single CloudWatch dashboard (C-13) covers infrastructure saturation metrics but the design does not describe regular review of business outcome metrics such as request resolution rates or notification delivery success. | Define a documented metric review cadence and add business KPI metrics (request throughput, notification success rate, resolution time) to the CloudWatch dashboard (C-13) so operational reviews are aligned to business outcomes. | C-13, REQ-17 |
| OPS10-BP07 Automate responses to events | Operational excellence | partial | Workload | CloudWatch alarms are defined but the design does not describe any automated response actions (e.g., ECS service scaling, SNS-triggered runbook via Systems Manager) triggered by those alarms; all responses appear to be manual. | Attach an SNS topic to the critical CloudWatch alarms (task CPU, RDS free storage, error rate) and wire at least the ECS task restart alarm to an EventBridge rule invoking an ECS UpdateService action to automate recovery. | C-13, C-04, REQ-17 |
| PERF03-BP04 Implement strategies to improve query performance in data store | Performance efficiency | partial | Workload | The design relies on PostgreSQL's native query capabilities for the dashboard (ADR-002) but does not specify which indexes will be created on the maintenance requests table (e.g., on status, category, priority, created_at) to meet the 3-second query target (REQ-10) at 100,000 records. | Define the required PostgreSQL indexes (at minimum composite indexes on (status, created_at), (category, created_at), and (priority, created_at)) in the database migration scripts for C-07 to ensure the dashboard query SLA is met. | C-07, REQ-10, ADR-002 |
| PERF03-BP05 Implement data access patterns that utilize caching | Performance efficiency | partial | Workload | ASM-08 assumes PostgreSQL on db.t4g.micro can meet the 3-second dashboard query target without caching, but this has not been validated; repeated identical dashboard queries from 5 administrators could cause unnecessary RDS load. | Validate the dashboard query performance with a 100,000-record test dataset on db.t4g.micro, and if p95 latency exceeds 3 seconds, add an in-process cache (e.g., application-level TTL cache in C-04) for dashboard aggregation results with a 60-second TTL. | C-07, C-04, REQ-10, ASM-08 |
| REL01-BP04 Monitor and manage quotas | Reliability | partial | Workload | CloudWatch alarms cover resource saturation (CPU, memory, free storage) but there is no monitoring of service quota utilization (e.g., SES sending rate, Fargate task count vs. account quota) to provide early warning before limits are reached. | Add CloudWatch alarms using the AWS Service Quotas integration (or custom metrics) to alert when SES daily sending quota and Fargate running task count approach 80% of their respective limits. | C-13, REQ-08 |
| REL03-BP03 Provide service contracts per API | Reliability | partial | Workload | The design describes the Portal API (C-04) as a REST API but does not define machine-readable API contracts (e.g., OpenAPI specification) or a versioning strategy for the internal API consumed by the browser frontend. | Publish an OpenAPI 3.x specification for the Portal API (C-04) and adopt a URL versioning strategy (e.g., /v1/) so that future breaking changes can be deployed without disrupting existing browser clients. | C-04, C-07, REQ-02 |
| REL04-BP04 Make mutating operations idempotent | Reliability | partial | Workload | The design generates unique request IDs (REQ-03) but does not describe idempotency controls on the request submission API endpoint to prevent duplicate requests from browser retries or network errors. | Implement a client-supplied idempotency key on the POST /requests endpoint in the Portal API (C-04), storing the key in the RDS database (C-07) to deduplicate retried submissions within a configurable window. | C-04, C-07, REQ-03 |
| REL06-BP04 Automate responses (Real-time processing and alarming) | Reliability | partial | Workload | CloudWatch alarms are defined but the design does not describe any automated response actions attached to them; all alarm responses appear to require manual operator intervention. | Attach an SNS topic to the ECS task CPU and error-rate alarms in C-13 and configure an EventBridge rule to invoke ECS UpdateService to increase the desired task count automatically when the CPU alarm fires. | C-13, C-04 |
| REL07-BP02 Obtain resources upon detection of impairment to a workload | Reliability | partial | Workload | The ECS service can scale to additional tasks (ADR-001) but the design does not describe a reactive scaling policy triggered by an availability impairment alarm (e.g., high error rate or task health check failure). | Configure an ECS service auto-scaling policy on the Application Load Balancer RequestCountPerTarget metric so that a spike in error rate or latency automatically triggers a scale-out before availability is impacted. | C-04, C-13, REQ-11 |
| REL07-BP03 Obtain resources upon detection that more resources are needed for a workload | Reliability | partial | Workload | The design states the ECS service can scale to additional tasks but does not define a scaling policy, target metric, or minimum/maximum task count to automatically provision resources when demand increases toward the 10,000 requests/month growth target. | Define an ECS Application Auto Scaling policy targeting ALB RequestCountPerTarget with a scale-out threshold, a minimum of 1 task, and a maximum of 3 tasks, to automatically meet demand growth without manual intervention. | C-04, REQ-08, REQ-09 |
| REL10-BP02 Automate recovery for components constrained to a single location | Reliability | partial | Workload | All components are constrained to us-east-1a; the design describes a snapshot-restore recovery path (ADR-007) but does not document a complete, tested rebuild runbook that achieves the 8-hour RTO for a full AZ failure. | Create and document an IaC-driven rebuild runbook (e.g., CloudFormation stack re-deploy + RDS snapshot restore) that has been timed against the 8-hour RTO target and is stored in a location accessible outside the affected AZ. | C-04, C-07, ADR-007, REQ-12 |
| REL11-BP05 Use static stability to prevent bimodal behavior | Reliability | partial | Workload | The single Fargate task (C-04) is sized for normal load; under a failure scenario where the task restarts, it must handle the same load with no pre-provisioned headroom, potentially exhibiting bimodal behavior during recovery. | Set the ECS service minimum healthy percent to 100% and desired count to at least 1 with a warm-up period configured in the auto-scaling policy, and document that the task size (0.5 vCPU / 1 GB) has been validated under peak load to ensure static stability. | C-04, C-07, REQ-11 |
| SEC04-BP04 Initiate remediation for non-compliant resources | Security | partial | Workload | CloudWatch alarms are defined for operational metrics, but the design does not describe automated remediation for non-compliant resources (e.g., auto-reverting a security group change that opens port 5432 publicly, or re-enabling S3 Block Public Access if disabled). | Add an AWS Config rule with an automatic SSM remediation document to detect and revert any security group change that exposes the RDS port (5432) or the app port (8080) beyond their intended source security groups. | C-13, C-01 |
| SEC05-BP03 Implement inspection-based protection | Security | partial | Workload | The WAF (C-01) inspects inbound HTTP traffic at the ALB, but there is no inspection of outbound traffic from the Fargate task (C-04) to SES, Cognito, or S3, and no network-layer inspection between the app and data subnets. | Add a VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager and Cognito to keep those flows private, and define a restrictive egress security group on C-04 that allows HTTPS only to the specific AWS service CIDR ranges or prefix lists, limiting the blast radius of a compromised container. | C-01, C-02, ADR-005 |
| SEC05-BP04 Automate network protection | Security | partial | Workload | The WAF web ACL and ALB are described as manually configured components; the design does not reference IaC (e.g., CloudFormation or Terraform) for the network protection stack. | Specify that all WAF rules, security groups, and ALB listener configurations are defined in IaC and deployed via a CI/CD pipeline, with policy-as-code checks (e.g., cfn-guard) to validate rule changes before deployment. | C-01, C-02, ADR-005 |
| SEC06-BP04 Validate software integrity | Security | partial | Workload | The design enables ECR scan-on-push but does not describe cryptographic signing of container images (e.g., AWS Signer or Notation) to verify that only approved images are deployed to the ECS service. | Implement image signing using AWS Signer with Notation on the ECR repository (C-05) and add an ECS task definition policy that rejects unsigned images, ensuring software integrity end-to-end. | C-05, C-04 |
| SEC06-BP05 Automate compute protection | Security | partial | Workload | The design relies on manual remediation of ECR scan findings; there is no automated pipeline action to block deployment of images with critical vulnerabilities or to replace a running task when a new CVE is discovered. | Add an EventBridge rule that triggers on ECR scan findings with CRITICAL severity and invokes a Lambda function (or Step Functions workflow) to notify the team and optionally stop the affected ECS task, forcing a redeployment from a patched image. | C-05, C-04, C-13 |
| SEC07-BP03 Automate identification and classification | Security | partial | Workload | Data classification is documented in the SRS (internal business data) but the design does not include any automated classification tool (e.g., Amazon Macie) to continuously verify that sensitive data in S3 (C-08) or RDS (C-07) conforms to the stated classification. | Enable Amazon Macie on the Export and Assets Bucket (C-08) to automatically detect and alert on any PII or sensitive data patterns in CSV exports that may exceed the stated internal classification. | C-07, C-08, REQ-13 |
| SUS02-BP01 Scale workload infrastructure dynamically | Sustainability | partial | Workload | The Fargate task runs at a fixed desired count of 1 with no auto-scaling policy defined, meaning the workload cannot scale down during off-hours (nights, weekends) to reduce resource consumption. | Define an ECS Application Auto Scaling policy with a minimum of 1 task and scale-in enabled, so that during low-demand periods the service operates at minimum capacity and reduces energy consumption. | C-04, ADR-001, REQ-08 |
| SUS02-BP06 Implement buffering or throttling to flatten the demand curve | Sustainability | partial | Workload | Email notifications are dispatched synchronously on every status change without any buffering; during burst periods (e.g., bulk status updates by maintenance staff), this creates unnecessary peak load on both the Fargate task and SES. | Introduce a short-lived notification buffer (e.g., an in-memory queue within C-04 or a lightweight SQS queue) to batch and smooth notification dispatch, reducing peak resource consumption. | C-04, C-09, REQ-05 |
| SUS03-BP01 Optimize software and architecture for asynchronous and scheduled jobs | Sustainability | partial | Workload | Notifications are dispatched synchronously within the request-handling path rather than as a scheduled or asynchronous job, preventing efficient resource utilization during burst periods. | Decouple notification dispatch from the synchronous API response path by persisting notification events to a table in RDS (C-07) and processing them asynchronously on a short polling interval within the Fargate task, improving resource utilization. | C-04, C-09, REQ-05 |
| SUS03-BP02 Remove or refactor workload components with low or no use | Sustainability | partial | Workload | The design does not describe a process for reviewing component utilization after go-live to identify and remove underutilized resources (e.g., if the db.t4g.micro is consistently at 5% CPU, a smaller or serverless option may be more efficient). | Schedule a utilization review 60 days after go-live using AWS Compute Optimizer and RDS Performance Insights to identify and right-size or remove underutilized components in C-04 and C-07. | C-04, C-07, REQ-15 |

Platform findings need a landing-zone revision; they are not applied by revising this design.

## 3. Resolved since the previous version

None.

## 4. Project constraints

None.

## 5. Accepted risks

None.

## 6. Not assessed at design stage

139 best practices are team or operating practices that a design cannot show. They are reviewed with the customer's teams, not from this design. Questions with no design-scope best practice:
- OPS 1. How do you determine what your priorities are?
- OPS 2. How do you structure your organization to support your business outcomes?
- OPS 3. How does your organizational culture support your business outcomes?
- OPS 6. How do you mitigate deployment risks?
- OPS 7. How do you know that you are ready to support a workload?
- OPS 9. How do you understand the health of your operations?
- OPS 11. How do you evolve operations?
- SEC 10. How do you anticipate, respond to, and recover from incidents?
- SEC 11. How do you incorporate and validate the security properties of applications throughout the design, development, and deployment lifecycle?
- REL 12. How do you test reliability?
- COST 1. How do you implement cloud financial management?
- COST 10. How do you evaluate new services?
- COST 11. How do you evaluate the cost of effort?
- SUS 6. How do your organizational processes support your sustainability goals?

## 7. Assessed at the landing-zone stage

The account structure and organization-wide controls are generated after this version is approved, as the landing zone and its IaC. The solution architect judges these best practices there; they are not scored here.

| Best practice | Pillar | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| OPS05-BP08 Use multiple environments | Operational excellence | Medium |
| SEC01-BP01 Separate workloads using accounts | Security | High |
| SEC01-BP02 Secure account root user and properties | Security | High |
| SEC01-BP05 Reduce security management scope | Security | Medium |
| SEC01-BP06 Automate deployment of standard security controls | Security | Medium |
| COST02-BP03 Implement an account structure | Cost optimization | High |
| COST02-BP05 Implement cost controls | Cost optimization | Medium |

## 8. Warnings

None.

## 9. Method

A model judged every design-scope best practice of the framework snapshot against the SRS and the design (met, partial, not met, not applicable, constraint). Code then applied the project constraints and the risks the architect accepted, and computed every number in this report. Issue risk is the framework's risk level for a best practice that is not met, one level lower when it is partly met. The score of a pillar is (met + half of partial) divided by the best practices judged met, partial or not met. This is a design-stage review for the solution architect; it does not replace a Well-Architected review of the running workload.
