# Architecture Decision Record: Equipment Maintenance Request Portal

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Customer | Northstar Facilities Group |
| Status | Proposed |
| Date | 2026-10-30 |
| Region | us-east-1 |
| Availability Zones | us-east-1a |
| DR Region | None |
| Source document | Equipment Maintenance Request Portal |
| Components | 17 |

## 1. Context

Northstar Facilities Group manages commercial office buildings and currently handles equipment maintenance requests via email and spreadsheets. This portal replaces that process with a web application supporting 525 users (employees, maintenance staff, and administrators) across request submission, assignment, status tracking, email notifications, and operational reporting. The system runs in a single AZ (us-east-1a) by explicit customer choice, targets 99.0% monthly availability, must stay within USD 100/month, and must retain all request records and audit history for 3 years. No external identity provider is required; no DR Region is provisioned.

## 2. Requirements addressed

| ID | Requirement | Type |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-01 | The system shall allow employees to sign in using company email credentials with role-based access control. | functional |
| REQ-02 | The system shall allow employees to submit, view, and comment on maintenance requests with title, description, location, category, and priority. | functional |
| REQ-03 | The system shall generate a unique request ID for every submitted request and record timestamps and user identity for every status change. | functional |
| REQ-04 | The system shall allow maintenance staff to view all open requests, assign them to personnel, and update statuses through the workflow: Submitted, Assigned, In Progress, Resolved, Closed. | functional |
| REQ-05 | The system shall send an email notification within 60 seconds of a status change. | functional |
| REQ-06 | The system shall provide a dashboard showing request counts by status, category, and priority, and allow administrators to export filtered records as UTF-8 CSV files (up to 10,000 records). | functional |
| REQ-07 | The system shall allow administrators to create, disable, and reactivate user accounts. | functional |
| REQ-08 | The system shall support 525 registered users and 2,000 maintenance requests per month, with a growth path to 10,000 requests per month. | non_functional |
| REQ-09 | 95% of request submission operations shall complete within 2 seconds under 50 concurrent users. | non_functional |
| REQ-10 | 95% of dashboard queries shall complete within 3 seconds for a dataset of 100,000 requests. | non_functional |
| REQ-11 | The system shall target 99.0% monthly availability within a single-AZ deployment in us-east-1a. | non_functional |
| REQ-12 | The recovery point objective shall be 24 hours and the recovery time objective shall be 8 hours. | non_functional |
| REQ-13 | Request records, comments, and audit history shall be retained for 3 years; expired records shall be deleted within 30 days after the retention period ends. | non_functional |
| REQ-14 | All data in transit shall use TLS 1.2 or later and access shall enforce role-based authorization. | non_functional |
| REQ-15 | Total AWS infrastructure expenditure shall remain below USD 100 per month. | constraint |
| REQ-16 | All zonal resources must reside in us-east-1a; the application must use AWS-native managed services only; no third-party SaaS for core request processing. | constraint |
| REQ-17 | Application errors, failed notifications, and request-processing failures shall be logged and retained for 30 days. | non_functional |
| REQ-18 | A qualified engineer shall be able to deploy a routine application update within 30 minutes using documented procedures. | non_functional |

## 3. Architecture decisions

### ADR-001: Use AWS Fargate (single task) for the application API and web serving

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The portal serves 525 users with at most 50 concurrent users (REQ-08, REQ-09). The SRS mandates a single-AZ deployment (REQ-11, REQ-16) and a USD 100/month cost ceiling (REQ-15). A long-running web/API service with persistent HTTP connections is needed. The deployment must be updatable within 30 minutes (REQ-18).

**Decision:** Use one AWS Fargate task (Linux/ARM64, 0.5 vCPU / 1 GB) in the private-app subnet of us-east-1a. A single task is sufficient for the stated concurrency; the ECS service can scale to additional tasks if load grows. Container images are stored in Amazon ECR.

**Consequences:**
- Graviton ARM64 minimises compute cost, keeping the design within the USD 100 budget.
- A single task means no redundancy within the AZ; a task failure causes a brief outage until ECS restarts it (consistent with the 99.0% availability target).
- Scaling to 10,000 requests/month (REQ-08) is achieved by increasing the desired task count without workflow changes.
- Deployments via ECS rolling update satisfy the 30-minute update requirement (REQ-18).

**Requirements:** REQ-08, REQ-09, REQ-11, REQ-15, REQ-16, REQ-18

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** AWS Lambda for the API (Lambda cold starts and the 15-minute execution limit are unsuitable for a stateful web session and streaming CSV exports up to 10,000 rows (REQ-06); Lambda would also require API Gateway, adding cost.); Amazon EC2 t4g.micro (EC2 requires OS patching and AMI management, violating the managed-services constraint (REQ-16), and a t4g.micro has only 1 GiB RAM which is the same as the Fargate task but with higher operational overhead.)

### ADR-002: Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ for request and audit data

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The data model is relational: requests, assignments, comments, and audit events require joins and transactions (REQ-03, REQ-10). The dashboard must query 100,000 records within 3 seconds (REQ-10). The SRS mandates single-AZ deployment (REQ-16) and a 24-hour RPO / 8-hour RTO (REQ-12). The cost ceiling is USD 100/month (REQ-15).

**Decision:** Use one Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 Single-AZ instance, db.t4g.micro, gp3 20 GiB, 7-day automated backups with point-in-time recovery, encrypted with the customer managed KMS key, placed in the private-data subnet of us-east-1a.

**Consequences:**
- Automated daily snapshots and PITR satisfy the 24-hour RPO; restoring a snapshot to a new instance satisfies the 8-hour RTO.
- Single-AZ means a hardware failure requires a snapshot restore, which is accepted per the 99.0% availability target and customer sign-off.
- db.t4g.micro (2 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM) is the smallest Graviton RDS size; move to db.t4g.small when average CPU exceeds 70% or free memory drops below 200 MiB.
- PostgreSQL full-text search and window functions satisfy the dashboard query requirement without a separate analytics service.

**Requirements:** REQ-03, REQ-10, REQ-12, REQ-13, REQ-15, REQ-16

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Amazon DynamoDB (Dashboard queries (REQ-10) require aggregations and joins across requests, assignments, and audit events that are natural in SQL but expensive to model in DynamoDB.); Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 (Aurora's minimum cost (0.5 ACU minimum) exceeds the db.t4g.micro price and would push the design over the USD 100 budget (REQ-15).)

### ADR-003: Use Amazon Cognito for user authentication and RBAC

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The portal requires email-and-password sign-in for 525 users with three roles (employee, maintenance staff, administrator) and no external identity provider (REQ-01, REQ-07, REQ-14). The solution must use AWS-native managed services (REQ-16).

**Decision:** Use one Amazon Cognito user pool (Essentials tier) with email-and-password authentication. Three Cognito groups map to the three application roles. The application validates the JWT issued by Cognito on every API request to enforce RBAC.

**Consequences:**
- Cognito's free tier (50,000 MAUs) covers the 525-user base at zero incremental cost, supporting the USD 100 budget.
- Administrators manage user accounts (create, disable, reactivate) via the Cognito admin API called from the application (REQ-07).
- Password reset and account recovery are handled natively by Cognito, reducing application code.
- If Northstar later requires SAML federation, Cognito supports it without replacing the authentication layer.

**Requirements:** REQ-01, REQ-07, REQ-14, REQ-16

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Custom JWT authentication in the application (Building and maintaining a secure credential store violates the managed-services constraint (REQ-16) and introduces security risk.)

### ADR-004: Use Amazon SES for email status notifications

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The system must send email notifications within 60 seconds of a status change (REQ-05). The SRS requires an AWS-native service and no third-party SaaS (REQ-16). The customer provides a verified company email domain (Section 2.5).

**Decision:** Use Amazon SES with one verified domain identity and DKIM enabled. The application API calls SES directly via the AWS SDK on each status-change event. SES delivery failures are logged to CloudWatch.

**Consequences:**
- SES sends email within seconds of the API call, satisfying the 60-second notification requirement.
- SES sandbox mode must be exited before go-live; the customer must verify the sending domain (OI-02).
- SES is a regional service with no VPC placement required; the Fargate task reaches it via the NAT Gateway.
- Bounces and complaints are handled via SES event notifications to CloudWatch.

**Requirements:** REQ-05, REQ-16

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Amazon SNS email subscriptions (SNS email is intended for operational alerts, not transactional application notifications; it does not support HTML templates or per-recipient personalisation needed for status notifications.)

### ADR-005: Use Application Load Balancer with AWS WAF as the public entry point

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The platform contract mandates a per-workload WAF and a distributed ingress pattern with the ALB in the public tier (ingress: distributed, waf: per-workload). All browser communications must use HTTPS (REQ-14, C-03). The ALB terminates TLS and forwards to the Fargate task.

**Decision:** Deploy one internet-facing Application Load Balancer (single_az in us-east-1a, the only AZ in this deployment) with an HTTPS 443 listener and an ACM certificate. Attach one AWS WAF web ACL (AWS managed Core Rule Set, Known Bad Inputs, and one rate-based rule) to the ALB.

**Consequences:**
- TLS termination at the ALB enforces HTTPS for all browser traffic (REQ-14).
- WAF protects against common web exploits and rate-based abuse without additional cost beyond the WAF ACL and rule charges.
- The ALB and WAF are the only components in the public subnet; all application and data resources remain private.
- ALB access logs provide an audit trail of all inbound requests.

**Requirements:** REQ-14, REQ-15, REQ-16

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Amazon API Gateway HTTP API (API Gateway adds per-request cost and is optimised for REST/HTTP APIs rather than serving a full web application with file downloads and session-based flows; ALB is more cost-effective at this scale.)

### ADR-006: Use Amazon S3 for CSV exports and static assets with lifecycle retention

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** Administrators export filtered request records as CSV files up to 10,000 rows (REQ-06). Request records and audit history must be retained for 3 years and deleted within 30 days after expiry (REQ-13). A cost-effective object store is needed (REQ-15).

**Decision:** Use one Amazon S3 bucket for CSV exports and application static assets. Enable SSE-KMS encryption, versioning, and Block Public Access. Apply an S3 lifecycle rule to transition objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days and expire them after 3 years plus 30 days (1,125 days total).

**Consequences:**
- Lifecycle rules automate the 3-year retention and 30-day deletion window (REQ-13) without manual intervention.
- Pre-signed URLs generated by the API allow secure browser downloads without making the bucket public.
- S3 Standard storage cost for the expected export volume is negligible within the USD 100 budget.
- Glacier transition reduces long-term storage cost for aged exports.

**Requirements:** REQ-06, REQ-13, REQ-15

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Serving CSV directly from the database via the API response stream (Streaming large exports through the Fargate task ties up the task for the duration of the download and does not provide durable storage or audit of exported files.)

### ADR-007: Use AWS Backup for automated database snapshots to meet RPO/RTO

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** The RPO is 24 hours and the RTO is 8 hours (REQ-12). The deployment is single-AZ with no DR Region (REQ-16, contract). The customer must approve the backup and recovery procedure (OI-03).

**Decision:** Use AWS Backup with a daily backup plan targeting the RDS instance, a 7-day retention window in the primary vault, and a backup window of 02:00–03:00 UTC. RDS automated backups (7-day retention, PITR) are also enabled as a secondary recovery path.

**Consequences:**
- Daily snapshots satisfy the 24-hour RPO; restoring a snapshot to a new db.t4g.micro instance in us-east-1a satisfies the 8-hour RTO.
- AWS Backup provides centralised visibility and policy-driven compliance reporting for OI-03.
- Snapshot storage cost is minimal for a 20 GiB database.
- A hardware failure in the single AZ requires a restore; there is no automatic failover.

**Requirements:** REQ-12, REQ-13, REQ-15

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** RDS automated backups only (no AWS Backup) (AWS Backup provides a centralised audit trail and policy enforcement required by the customer's information security policy (NFR-11); RDS automated backups alone do not satisfy the compliance reporting need.)

### ADR-008: Add CloudWatch Synthetics canaries for user experience telemetry

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** Addresses OPS04-BP03. The design had no real user monitoring or synthetic transaction capability; user-facing performance issues such as slow page loads or failed submissions would only be detected through user reports or backend error logs. Proactive detection of user-facing availability and performance degradations is required to meet the 99.0% availability target (REQ-11) and the 2-second submission performance target (REQ-09).

**Decision:** Add one Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canary group with three canaries (Node.js 18.x runtime): one simulating login, one simulating request submission, and one simulating dashboard load. Canaries run every 5 minutes and publish pass/fail metrics and screenshots to CloudWatch. Alarms are configured on canary failure counts.

**Consequences:**
- Proactive detection of user-facing failures before users report them, supporting the 99.0% availability target.
- Canary screenshots and HAR files provide evidence for diagnosing performance regressions.
- Three canaries running every 5 minutes add a small but predictable cost; at this frequency the cost is well within the USD 100 budget.
- Canary scripts must be updated when the application UI changes, adding a small maintenance burden.

**Requirements:** REQ-09, REQ-11, REQ-17

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Amazon CloudWatch RUM (real user monitoring) (RUM requires injecting a JavaScript snippet into the application and collects data only when real users are active; synthetic canaries provide continuous coverage even during off-hours and are simpler to configure for a small portal.)

### ADR-009: Enable AWS X-Ray distributed tracing on the Portal API

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** Addresses OPS04-BP05. The design had no distributed tracing; there was no visibility into end-to-end latency or errors across the Portal API's (C-04) calls to RDS (C-07), SES (C-09), Cognito (C-06), S3 (C-08), and Secrets Manager (C-12). Distributed tracing is required to diagnose performance issues and satisfy the observability requirements (REQ-17).

**Decision:** Enable AWS X-Ray active tracing on the ECS task definition for the Portal API (C-04). Instrument the application using the AWS X-Ray SDK to trace all downstream SDK calls to RDS, SES, Cognito, S3, and Secrets Manager. The X-Ray daemon runs as a sidecar container in the same ECS task. Traces are retained for 30 days in X-Ray.

**Consequences:**
- End-to-end request traces provide visibility into latency contributions from each downstream dependency.
- X-Ray service map automatically visualises the call graph between the Portal API and its dependencies.
- The X-Ray daemon sidecar adds a small memory overhead to the Fargate task; the existing 1 GB allocation is sufficient.
- X-Ray trace data is sampled at the default rate (5% after the first request per second); this is sufficient for a low-traffic portal and keeps cost negligible.

**Requirements:** REQ-17, REQ-16

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** OpenTelemetry with a third-party backend (A third-party tracing backend would violate the AWS-native managed services constraint (REQ-16) and add cost; AWS X-Ray integrates natively with ECS and the AWS SDK.)

### ADR-010: Configure explicit SDK retry, backoff, and timeout settings in the Portal API

**Status:** Accepted

**Context:** Addresses REL05-BP03 and REL05-BP05. The design did not describe retry logic or timeout values for the Portal API's (C-04) calls to RDS (C-07), SES (C-09), Secrets Manager (C-12), or S3 (C-08). AWS SDK defaults may not be appropriate for a single Fargate task where hung or endlessly retrying requests could exhaust the task's capacity and violate the 2-second submission performance target (REQ-09).

**Decision:** Configure the Portal API application with explicit AWS SDK retry and timeout settings: exponential backoff with full jitter and a maximum of 3 retries for SES, S3, and Secrets Manager SDK calls; RDS connection timeout of 5 seconds and statement timeout of 30 seconds via PostgreSQL connection string parameters; SES SDK call timeout of 3 seconds; Secrets Manager SDK call timeout of 2 seconds. These values are externalised as environment variables in the ECS task definition.

**Consequences:**
- Explicit timeouts prevent hung requests from blocking the single Fargate task and degrading all concurrent users.
- Exponential backoff with jitter reduces thundering-herd retries against downstream services during transient failures.
- A maximum of 3 retries balances resilience against the 60-second notification SLA (REQ-05) and the 2-second submission target (REQ-09).
- Externalising timeout values as environment variables allows tuning without a container image rebuild.

**Requirements:** REQ-09, REQ-05, REQ-11

**Alternatives considered (rejected, not part of this design):** Rely on AWS SDK default retry and timeout behaviour (SDK defaults (e.g., unlimited retries with fixed backoff in some SDK versions) can cause request pile-up on a single Fargate task and are not documented as appropriate for this workload's latency and concurrency constraints.)

## 4. Network layout

The solution runs in AWS Region us-east-1. It uses one VPC, Prod VPC, in Availability Zone us-east-1a. The Public subnets (public) use 10.0.0.0/24 in us-east-1a. The App subnets (private-app) use 10.0.1.0/24 in us-east-1a. The Data subnets (private-data) use 10.0.2.0/24 in us-east-1a. The Prod VPC contains the VPC Endpoints. The Public subnets, in Prod VPC, contains the Web Application Firewall, the Application Load Balancer and the NAT Gateway. The App subnets, in Prod VPC, contains the Portal API. The Data subnets, in Prod VPC, contains the Request Database. Region-level services used: Container Registry, User Pool, Export and Assets Bucket, Email Notification Service, Backup Plan, Encryption Key, Secrets Store, Observability, Synthetics Canaries and Distributed Tracing. Outside AWS, the solution involves: Portal Users.

### Platform contract

The approved landing zone fixes these values; the design places its components inside them.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Account | northstar-maintenance-portal-prod |
| Organizational unit | Workloads/Prod |
| Region | us-east-1 |
| Availability Zones | us-east-1a |
| Prod VPC | 10.0.0.0/20 (us-east-1) |
| Public subnets (public) | 10.0.0.0/24 |
| App subnets (private-app) | 10.0.1.0/24 |
| Data subnets (private-data) | 10.0.2.0/24 |
| DR Region | None |
| Connectivity | none |
| Egress | local-nat |
| Ingress | distributed, WAF per-workload |
| Provided by the platform | AWS CloudTrail, AWS Config, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, AWS IAM Access Analyzer, AWS IAM Identity Center |
| Landing-zone version | version 1 (f9fff5e1fd38f60b) |

## 5. Components

| ID | Component | AWS service | SKU / configuration | Qty | Placement | AZ placement | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-00 | Portal Users | Users (Employees, Maintenance Staff, Administrators) | 525 users across three roles | 1 | External | External | Employees submit and track requests; maintenance staff assign and resolve requests; administrators manage users and generate reports. |
| C-01 | Web Application Firewall | AWS WAF | 1 web ACL, Core Rule Set + Known Bad Inputs + 1 rate-based rule, attached to ALB | 1 | Public subnets | Single AZ (us-east-1a) | Protects the public entry point against common web exploits and rate-based abuse as required by the platform contract. |
| C-02 | Application Load Balancer | Application Load Balancer | Internet-facing ALB, HTTPS 443, ACM certificate, targets Fargate tasks | 1 | Public subnets | Single AZ (us-east-1a) | Terminates TLS and forwards HTTPS requests from browsers to the Portal API Fargate task. |
| C-03 | NAT Gateway | NAT Gateway | 1 public NAT Gateway in us-east-1a | 1 | Public subnets | Single AZ (us-east-1a) | Provides outbound internet access for the Fargate task to reach Amazon SES and other AWS regional endpoints not covered by VPC gateway endpoints. |
| C-04 | Portal API | AWS Fargate | Fargate Linux/ARM64, 0.5 vCPU / 1 GB, 1 task in us-east-1a, X-Ray active tracing enabled | 1 | App subnets | Single AZ (us-east-1a) | Runs the stateless web application and REST API: handles request submission, status updates, assignment, comments, user management, dashboard queries, and CSV export generation; instrumented with X-Ray and configured with explicit SDK retry and timeout settings. |
| C-05 | Container Registry | Amazon ECR | Private ECR repository, scan on push, lifecycle keeps last 10 images | 1 | Region | Regional | Stores and versions the Portal API container image used by the ECS service. |
| C-06 | User Pool | Amazon Cognito | Cognito user pool, Essentials tier, email/password auth, 3 groups | 1 | Region | Regional | Authenticates all 525 users with email and password, issues JWTs, and enforces role-based access via Cognito groups for employee, maintenance staff, and administrator roles. |
| C-07 | Request Database | Amazon RDS | db.t4g.micro, PostgreSQL 17, gp3 20 GiB, Single-AZ, 7-day backups | 1 | Data subnets | Single AZ (us-east-1a) | System of record for all maintenance requests, assignments, comments, audit events, and user data; supports dashboard aggregation queries and CSV export filtering. |
| C-08 | Export and Assets Bucket | Amazon S3 | S3 Standard, SSE-KMS, versioning on, lifecycle to Glacier at 90 days, expiry at 1125 days | 1 | Region | Regional | Stores administrator CSV exports (served via pre-signed URLs) and application static assets; lifecycle rules enforce the 3-year retention and 30-day deletion window. |
| C-09 | Email Notification Service | Amazon SES | SES verified domain identity, DKIM on, shared IP, 1 configuration set | 1 | Region | Regional | Delivers transactional email notifications to requesters within 60 seconds of a status change event triggered by the Portal API. |
| C-10 | Backup Plan | AWS Backup | AWS Backup daily plan, 7-day retention, targeting RDS instance | 1 | Region | Regional | Provides centralised, policy-driven daily snapshots of the RDS instance to satisfy the 24-hour RPO and compliance reporting requirements. |
| C-11 | Encryption Key | AWS KMS | 1 customer managed symmetric KMS key, annual rotation | 1 | Region | Regional | Encrypts the RDS database and S3 bucket at rest with a customer managed key, satisfying the information security policy. |
| C-12 | Secrets Store | AWS Secrets Manager | 1 secret for RDS credentials, automatic rotation every 30 days | 1 | Region | Regional | Stores and rotates the RDS master credentials used by the Portal API, eliminating hard-coded secrets. |
| C-13 | Observability | Amazon CloudWatch | CloudWatch log groups (30-day retention), 1 dashboard, alarms on errors, saturation, and canary failures | 1 | Region | Regional | Collects application logs, ECS task metrics, RDS metrics, and Synthetics canary results; raises alarms on errors, failed notifications, resource saturation, and canary failures; provides the operational dashboard. |
| C-14 | VPC Endpoints | AWS PrivateLink | S3 gateway endpoint for the Prod VPC | 1 | Prod VPC | Regional | Routes S3 traffic from the Fargate task and RDS backups through the S3 gateway endpoint, avoiding NAT Gateway data charges for S3 access. |
| C-15 | Synthetics Canaries | Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics | 3 CloudWatch Synthetics canaries (Node.js/Puppeteer), 5-minute schedule, 30-day artifact retention | 1 | Region | Regional | Simulates login, request submission, and dashboard load flows every 5 minutes to proactively detect user-facing availability and performance degradations before users report them. |
| C-16 | Distributed Tracing | AWS X-Ray | X-Ray active tracing, default sampling, 30-day retention, X-Ray daemon as ECS sidecar | 1 | Region | Regional | Provides end-to-end distributed tracing for all Portal API requests, capturing latency and error data across calls to RDS, SES, Cognito, S3, and Secrets Manager. |

## 6. Request and data flow

1. Portal Users send HTTPS requests to the Application Load Balancer on port 443. (F-01; HTTPS 443)
2. The Application Load Balancer passes all inbound requests through the Web Application Firewall before forwarding them. (F-02; HTTPS 443)
3. The Application Load Balancer forwards inspected HTTPS requests to the Portal API Fargate task on port 8080. (F-03; HTTP 8080)
4. The Portal API validates Cognito-issued JWTs against the User Pool to authenticate and authorise every request. (F-04; HTTPS 443)
5. The Portal API retrieves RDS credentials from the Secrets Store at startup and on rotation. (F-05; HTTPS 443)
6. The Portal API reads and writes maintenance requests, assignments, comments, and audit events in the Request Database. (F-06; PostgreSQL 5432)
7. The Portal API calls the Email Notification Service via the AWS SDK to send status-change emails to requesters. (F-07; HTTPS 443)
8. The Portal API writes generated CSV export files to the Export and Assets Bucket and returns a pre-signed URL to the administrator. (F-08; HTTPS 443)
9. Portal Users (administrators) download CSV export files directly from the Export and Assets Bucket using a pre-signed URL. (F-09; HTTPS 443)
10. The Backup Plan takes a daily snapshot of the Request Database and stores it in the AWS Backup vault. (F-10; AWS internal N/A)
11. The Portal API emits application logs and custom metrics to Observability (CloudWatch) for error tracking and alerting. (F-11; HTTPS 443)
12. The Portal API sends X-Ray trace segments to the Distributed Tracing service via the X-Ray daemon sidecar for end-to-end request tracing. (F-12; UDP 2000)
13. The Synthetics Canaries send synthetic HTTPS requests to the Application Load Balancer every 5 minutes to verify login, submission, and dashboard flows. (F-13; HTTPS 443)
14. The Synthetics Canaries publish pass/fail metrics and artifacts to Observability (CloudWatch) for alarming and dashboarding. (F-14; HTTPS 443)

## 7. Security and operations

- All inbound traffic enters exclusively through the Application Load Balancer (C-02) on port 443; the WAF (C-01) inspects every request before it reaches the Portal API (C-04). Security groups allow port 443 inbound only from 0.0.0.0/0 on the ALB; the Portal API security group allows port 8080 only from the ALB security group; the Request Database security group allows port 5432 only from the Portal API security group.
- All data at rest is encrypted: the Request Database (C-07) and Export and Assets Bucket (C-08) use the customer managed KMS key (C-11) via SSE-KMS. S3 Block Public Access is enabled on C-08.
- All data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or higher: HTTPS is enforced at the ALB (C-02); the Portal API (C-04) communicates with AWS services over TLS; the RDS connection uses SSL with certificate verification.
- The Portal API (C-04) runs under a least-privilege IAM role scoped to: read from Secrets Manager (C-12), send email via SES (C-09), read/write the S3 bucket (C-08), write CloudWatch logs (C-13), and send X-Ray trace segments (C-16). No wildcard actions or resource ARNs are permitted.
- RDS master credentials are stored in Secrets Manager (C-12) with automatic rotation every 30 days. No long-lived access keys are used anywhere in the workload.
- Amazon Cognito (C-06) issues short-lived JWTs; the Portal API validates the token signature and group membership on every API call to enforce RBAC across employee, maintenance staff, and administrator roles.
- CloudWatch (C-13) retains all application and infrastructure logs for 30 days. Alarms are configured on application error rates, failed SES notifications, ECS task CPU and memory, RDS CPU and free storage, and Synthetics canary failure counts.
- AWS CloudTrail (provided by platform) records all API calls across the account. The S3 gateway endpoint (C-14) ensures S3 traffic does not traverse the public internet.
- The ECR repository (C-05) has scan-on-push enabled; critical vulnerabilities must be remediated before deploying a new image. The ECS task definition uses read-only root filesystem and drops all Linux capabilities not required by the application.
- AWS Backup (C-10) enforces a backup vault lock policy preventing deletion of snapshots within the 7-day retention window, supporting the RPO of 24 hours and the customer's information security policy.
- AWS X-Ray (C-16) active tracing is enabled on the Portal API ECS task definition; the X-Ray daemon runs as a sidecar container. The Portal API IAM role grants xray:PutTraceSegments and xray:PutTelemetryRecords only. Trace data is retained for 30 days.
- The Portal API (C-04) enforces explicit connection and SDK call timeouts (5 s RDS connect, 30 s RDS statement, 3 s SES, 2 s Secrets Manager) and uses exponential backoff with full jitter and a maximum of 3 retries for all downstream SDK calls, preventing hung requests from exhausting the single Fargate task.

## 8. Assumptions

| ID | Assumption | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| ASM-01 | The Portal API container listens on port 8080 and the ALB target group is configured accordingly. | The SRS does not specify an application port; 8080 is the conventional non-privileged HTTP port for containerised web applications. |
| ASM-02 | MFA is optional (not enforced) in the Cognito user pool. | The SRS requires email-and-password authentication (Section 5) but does not mandate MFA; optional MFA allows administrators to enable it later without a design change. |
| ASM-03 | The RDS instance uses db.t4g.micro (2 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM), the smallest Graviton RDS size. | The SRS data volumes (525 users, 100,000 requests over the operating period) are modest; db.t4g.micro is the most cost-effective choice to stay within the USD 100/month budget (REQ-15). Upgrade to db.t4g.small when average CPU exceeds 70% or free memory drops below 200 MiB. |
| ASM-04 | The Fargate task uses 0.5 vCPU and 1 GB memory, the smallest valid Fargate configuration. | 50 concurrent users (REQ-09) with a stateless API is well within the capacity of a single small Fargate task; this minimises cost (REQ-15). |
| ASM-05 | SES is used in the us-east-1 region and the customer will exit SES sandbox mode before go-live. | SES sandbox mode restricts sending to verified addresses only; production use requires sandbox exit, which depends on the customer verifying their domain (OI-02). |
| ASM-06 | The S3 lifecycle expiration is set to 1,125 days (3 years × 365 days + 30 days grace period) to satisfy the retention and deletion requirements. | REQ-13 requires 3-year retention and deletion within 30 days after expiry; 1,125 days covers both without manual intervention. |
| ASM-07 | The ACM certificate for the ALB is issued for the customer's domain and managed by ACM for automatic renewal. | The SRS requires HTTPS (C-03) but does not specify the domain name; ACM-managed certificates eliminate manual renewal overhead. |
| ASM-08 | No ElastiCache or query caching layer is added for dashboard queries. | PostgreSQL with appropriate indexes on a db.t4g.micro can satisfy the 3-second dashboard query target (REQ-10) for 100,000 records; a cache would add cost that risks breaching the USD 100 budget (REQ-15). |
| ASM-09 | The Synthetics canaries use the syn-nodejs-puppeteer-9.0 runtime and run from the us-east-1 region. | The SRS does not specify a synthetic monitoring runtime; syn-nodejs-puppeteer-9.0 is the current stable CloudWatch Synthetics runtime supporting full browser simulation for login and form flows. |
| ASM-10 | The X-Ray daemon sidecar container uses 64 MiB memory, allocated from within the existing 1 GB Fargate task memory. | The SRS does not specify sidecar resource allocation; 64 MiB is the standard X-Ray daemon recommendation and leaves 960 MiB for the application container within the 1 GB task definition. |

## 9. Open questions

- OI-01 (from SRS): The final list of maintenance request categories must be confirmed by the Operations Director before application configuration.
- OI-02 (from SRS): The company email domain and SES sender verification requirements must be confirmed by the IT Administrator before go-live; SES sandbox exit depends on this.
- OI-03 (from SRS): The IT Administrator must formally approve the single-AZ backup and recovery procedure, including the expected 8-hour RTO via snapshot restore.
- OI-04 (from SRS): The Operations Director must confirm whether CSV exports exceeding 5,000 rows require additional approval, as this may require an application-level workflow gate.
- The ACM certificate domain name has not been specified in the SRS; the customer must provide the DNS name for the portal before the ALB listener can be configured.
- The SRS does not specify whether the Cognito user pool should enforce password complexity beyond AWS defaults; the customer's information security policy (NFR-11) should be reviewed to confirm.
- The Synthetics canary scripts require valid test user credentials for the login and request submission flows; the customer must confirm whether dedicated synthetic test accounts will be provisioned in the Cognito user pool or whether canaries will use a shared test account.

usage_assumptions.md.data:
# Usage estimate: Equipment Maintenance Request Portal

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Source document | srs.md |
| Date | 2026-10-30 |
| Model | us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 |
| Estimate | One expected month (no ranges) |
| Month length | 730 hours |
| Deployment | One Region (us-east-1), 1 Availability Zone (us-east-1a) |
| DR Region | None |
| Usage entries | 13 |
| Warnings | 6 |

## 1. Warnings

- C-10 (AWS Backup): AWS Backup is not in the tool schema and has been omitted from the usage file. It manages daily RDS snapshots with 7-day retention; the cost is driven by the RDS snapshot storage (~20 GB × 7 days).
- C-15 (Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics): CloudWatch Synthetics is not a separate service in the tool schema. Canary Lambda invocations (26,280 runs/month across 3 canaries) and artifact S3 storage are billed under CloudWatch Synthetics pricing, which is not captured in the CloudWatch entry above; the reader should add Synthetics canary run costs separately.
- C-16 (AWS X-Ray): AWS X-Ray is not in the tool schema and has been omitted from the usage file. At default sampling (~5% after the first request/second), estimated ~11,500 traces/month with ~5 segments each ≈ 57,500 recorded segments/month; the reader should price this separately.
- C-14 (AWS PrivateLink): The S3 gateway endpoint is free. The entry is included with zero billable usage to confirm coverage; no cost will be generated.
- REQ-15 / NFR-10: The SRS imposes a hard USD 100/month cost ceiling. The design is intentionally minimal (single-AZ, db.t4g.micro, 0.5 vCPU Fargate, shared SES IPs); the reader should verify the priced total remains below this constraint.
- C-13 and C-15 share the Amazon CloudWatch service; two entries are submitted under amazon_cloudwatch — one for C-13 (Observability) and one for C-15 (Synthetics Canaries) — because they represent distinct design components with separate log groups and usage patterns.

## 2. Workload profile

Every usage figure below is derived from these drivers. Basis: stated (in the SRS), inferred (calculated from stated numbers) or assumed (the SRS is silent).

| Driver | Value | Basis | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registered users | 525 users | stated | NFR-01: 'The system shall support 525 registered users and 2,000 maintenance requests per month.' |
| Monthly active users | 400 users/month | assumed | SRS states 525 registered users but does not specify how many are active each month. Assuming ~76% activity rate (400/525) is typical for an internal business tool where most employees interact occasionally. |
| Maintenance requests per month | 2000 requests/month | stated | NFR-01: '2,000 maintenance requests per month.' Also confirmed by data requirement: 24,000 new records annually ÷ 12 = 2,000/month. |
| Status changes per request | 3 status changes/request | assumed | FR-07 defines 5 statuses (Submitted, Assigned, In Progress, Resolved, Closed). A typical request transitions through ~3 changes on average (e.g., Submitted→Assigned→In Progress→Resolved). |
| Email notifications per month | 6000 emails/month | inferred | 2,000 requests × 3 status changes each = 6,000 notification emails per month (FR-09: one email per status change). |
| Comments per month | 5000 comments/month | inferred | Data requirement states 60,000 comment records annually ÷ 12 = 5,000 comments/month. |
| Audit events per month | 8333 events/month | inferred | Data requirement states 100,000 audit events annually ÷ 12 ≈ 8,333 events/month. |
| HTTP API requests per month | 150000 requests/month | assumed | Estimated from user activity: 400 MAU × ~10 sessions/month × ~35 API calls/session (page loads, submissions, status checks, comments, dashboard) ≈ 140,000; rounded to 150,000 to include canary synthetic traffic (3 canaries × 12/hr × 730 hr ≈ 26,280 canary runs, each ~3 API calls ≈ 79,000 additional calls). Total ≈ 150,000 human + 79,000 canary ≈ 230,000; using 150,000 as a conservative human-only baseline since canary calls are lightweight. |
| Synthetics canary runs per month | 26280 runs/month per canary | inferred | 3 canaries × (60/5) runs/hour × 730 hours/month = 3 × 12 × 730 = 26,280 total canary runs per month across all 3 canaries (8,760 per canary). |
| Database storage | 5 GB | assumed | At 2,000 requests/month with associated assignments, comments, and audit events, total annual records ≈ 194,000 rows. At ~2 KB average row size across all tables, 3 years of data ≈ 194,000 × 3 × 2 KB ≈ 1.2 GB. With indexes and overhead, ~5 GB is a comfortable estimate well within the 20 GB allocated. |
| S3 storage (CSV exports + static assets) | 1 GB | assumed | CSV exports: administrators export up to 10,000 records; at ~500 bytes/record a full export is ~5 MB. Assuming 10 exports/month stored for 90 days before Glacier transition = ~150 MB. Static assets (HTML, JS, CSS, images) ≈ 50 MB. Total ≈ 0.2 GB in Standard at steady state. |
| Log volume per month | 2 GB/month | assumed | One Fargate task at low traffic with X-Ray, ECS task logs, RDS PostgreSQL logs, and Synthetics canary artifacts. Estimated ~2 GB/month ingested across all log groups; typical for a lightly loaded single-task application. |
| X-Ray traces per month | 11500 traces/month | inferred | Default X-Ray sampling: first request per second is always sampled, then 5% of the remainder. At ~150,000 requests/month ÷ 730 hours ÷ 3600 seconds ≈ 0.057 req/s average, nearly every request is sampled (below 1 req/s threshold). Estimated ~150,000 × 5% + first-request sampling ≈ ~11,500 traces/month as a conservative figure given the low traffic rate. |

## 3. Usage by component

| Component | Service | Usage figures | How the figures were reached | Assumed fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-01 Web Application Firewall | AWS WAF | web_acl_count: 1; rules_per_acl: 3; requests_inspected_per_month: 229,000; managed_rule_groups: 2 | 1 web ACL with 2 managed rule groups (AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet, AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet) plus 1 rate-based rule = 3 rules. Requests inspected = ~150,000 human API requests + ~79,000 canary synthetic requests (3 canaries × 8,760 runs × ~3 HTTP calls each) ≈ 229,000 requests/month. | requests_inspected_per_month |
| C-03 NAT Gateway | NAT Gateway | gateway_count: 1; data_processed_gb: 1.5; availability_zones: 1 | 1 NAT Gateway in us-east-1a. Outbound traffic is primarily SES API calls (~6,000 emails × ~5 KB payload = ~30 MB) and ECR image pulls (~500 MB/month for deployments) plus SDK calls to Cognito and Secrets Manager. S3 traffic is routed via the gateway endpoint (C-14) and does not pass through NAT. Total estimated ~1.5 GB/month. | data_processed_gb |
| C-14 VPC Endpoints | AWS PrivateLink | endpoint_count: 0; data_processed_gb: 0; endpoint_type: Gateway | C-14 configures only an S3 gateway endpoint. Gateway endpoints for S3 are free and do not incur PrivateLink interface endpoint charges. The design explicitly states 'additional_interface_endpoints: none', so there are no billable interface endpoints. | none |
| C-02 Application Load Balancer | Application Load Balancer | load_balancer_count: 1; lcu_per_hour: 0.5; rules_count: 2; availability_zones: 1 | Single internet-facing ALB in us-east-1a with 1 HTTPS listener and ~2 rules (default + forward). At ~229,000 requests/month ÷ 730 hours ≈ 314 req/hr, well below 1 LCU threshold; estimated 0.5 LCU/hr to cover the minimum billing unit. | lcu_per_hour, rules_count |
| C-04 Portal API | AWS Fargate | vcpu_hours_per_month: 365; memory_gb_per_month: 730; operating_system: Linux; architecture: arm64 | 1 always-on task × 0.5 vCPU × 730 hours/month = 365 vCPU-hours. 1 task × 1 GB memory × 730 hours/month = 730 GB-hours. The X-Ray daemon sidecar (ASM-10) shares the 1 GB task memory allocation. | none |
| C-05 Container Registry | Amazon ECR | storage_gb: 2; data_transfer_out_gb: 0; repositories: 1; image_scans_per_month: 2 | 1 private repository with lifecycle policy keeping last 10 images. A Node.js/Go container image is typically 150–300 MB; 10 images ≈ 2 GB stored. Assuming ~2 image pushes (and scans) per month for routine deployments. Fargate pulls are within the same Region so data transfer out is $0. | storage_gb, image_scans_per_month |
| C-07 Request Database | Amazon RDS | engine: PostgreSQL; instance_class: db.t4g.micro; instance_count: 1; storage_gb: 20; multi_az: false; backup_retention_days: 7 | Single-AZ db.t4g.micro PostgreSQL 17 instance with 20 GB gp3 storage as specified in the design. Multi-AZ is explicitly false per the design and the SRS single-AZ constraint. 7-day automated backup retention as configured. | none |
| C-08 Export and Assets Bucket | Amazon S3 | storage_class: Standard; storage_gb: 0.5; get_requests_per_month: 15,000; put_requests_per_month: 500; data_transfer_out_gb: 0.5 | Stores CSV exports and static assets. At steady state ~0.5 GB in S3 Standard (objects transition to Glacier at 90 days). ~500 PUT requests/month (10 CSV exports + static asset deployments + versioning overhead). ~15,000 GET requests/month (static asset fetches by ~400 MAU × ~35 page loads + pre-signed URL downloads). ~0.5 GB data transfer out for CSV downloads by administrators (direct S3 pre-signed URL downloads to internet). | storage_gb, get_requests_per_month, put_requests_per_month, data_transfer_out_gb |
| C-09 Email Notification Service | Amazon SES | emails_per_month: 6,000; attachments_gb: 0; dedicated_ip: false; region: us-east-1 | 6,000 emails/month derived from 2,000 requests × 3 average status changes each (FR-09). Plain-text or HTML notifications with no attachments. Shared IP pool as configured in the design. | none |
| C-06 User Pool | Amazon Cognito | monthly_active_users: 400; user_pool_count: 1; advanced_security: false; mfa_enabled: false | 1 user pool (Essentials tier) with 525 registered users; estimated 400 MAU based on typical internal-tool engagement. MFA is optional per ASM-02 and the design configuration; advanced security is not configured (Essentials tier). | monthly_active_users |
| C-12 Secrets Store | AWS Secrets Manager | secrets_count: 1; api_calls_per_month: 50; rotation_enabled: true; rotation_frequency_days: 30 | 1 secret (RDS master credentials) with 30-day rotation. The Fargate task retrieves the secret at startup and caches it; with 1 task restarting infrequently, estimated ~50 GetSecretValue calls/month (task restarts + rotation Lambda calls + occasional health checks). | api_calls_per_month |
| C-11 Encryption Key | AWS KMS | customer_managed_keys: 1; api_calls_per_month: 15,000; key_type: Symmetric; multi_region: false | 1 symmetric CMK used for RDS SSE-KMS and S3 SSE-KMS. RDS generates a data key on startup and periodically; S3 uses Bucket Keys to reduce KMS calls. Estimated ~15,000 API calls/month: RDS connection/session key generation + S3 PUT/GET envelope encryption calls at low volume, plus Secrets Manager rotation calls. | api_calls_per_month |
| C-15 Synthetics Canaries | Amazon CloudWatch | metrics_per_month: 0; logs_ingested_gb_per_month: 0.5; log_storage_gb: 0.5; alarms_count: 0; dashboards_count: 0 | 3 Synthetics canaries running every 5 minutes = 8,760 runs/canary/month × 3 = 26,280 total runs. Canary artifacts (screenshots, HAR files) are stored for 30 days. Canary Lambda execution and artifact storage are billed under CloudWatch Synthetics. Log ingestion for canary results estimated ~0.5 GB/month. Alarms and dashboard are counted under C-13. | logs_ingested_gb_per_month |

## 4. Notes

- This is a very lightly loaded internal portal: 2,000 requests/month and ~400 MAU drive negligible compute and data transfer. The dominant cost drivers are the always-on RDS db.t4g.micro instance (730 hours/month), the always-on Fargate task (365 vCPU-hours + 730 GB-hours), the NAT Gateway hourly charge, and the 7 CloudWatch alarms plus 1 dashboard.
- The three CloudWatch Synthetics canaries (26,280 total runs/month) and X-Ray tracing are likely the next largest cost items but cannot be priced through this schema; the reader must add them manually.
- AWS Backup for RDS snapshots (7-day retention of a 20 GB database) adds a small but non-zero storage cost that is also outside the schema.
- The estimate would change most if: (a) the Fargate task is scaled out beyond 1 task, (b) the RDS instance is upgraded, or (c) the Synthetics canary frequency is increased — any of these could push the total toward or beyond the USD 100/month ceiling.

## 5. Method

- Configuration fields (instance class, engine, memory, storage size, counts) are copied from the ADR design; usage fields are estimated from the workload profile by one model call.
- One expected steady-state month of 730 hours. Prices, free tier and cost are left to the cost calculator.
- multi_az and availability_zones follow the design: the component's deployment configuration, its placement and AZs, and the design's Availability Zones. The estimate adds no standby, replica or AZ the design does not state. memory_gb is computed from memory_mb.
- Shared platform services (Transit Gateway, central inspection and egress, hub VPCs, the security and logging accounts) are not priced; the estimate covers this workload only.
- Components added later by the diagram's Assumer are not included; usage.json covers the ADR design only.

      "finding": "The design describes the Portal API (C-04) as a REST API but does not define machine-readable API contracts (e.g., OpenAPI specification) or a versioning strategy for the internal API consumed by the browser frontend.",
      "recommendation": "Publish an OpenAPI 3.0 specification for the Portal API (C-04) in the design, including a URL versioning strategy (e.g., /v1/), so that frontend and backend can evolve independently without breaking changes."

    {
      "bp_id": "REL04-BP04",
      "pillar": "Reliability",
      "question_id": "REL04",
      "question": "REL 4. How do you design interactions in a distributed system to prevent failures?",
      "title": "Make mutating operations idempotent",
      "risk": "Medium",
      "issue_risk": "Low",
      "status": "partial",
      "scope": "workload",
      "evidence_ids": [
        "C-04",
        "REQ-03",
        "REQ-02"
      ],
      "finding": "The design generates unique request IDs (REQ-03) but does not describe idempotency controls on the request submission API endpoint to prevent duplicate requests from browser retries or network errors.",
      "recommendation": "Add an idempotency key header to the request submission endpoint in the Portal API (C-04), backed by a short-lived deduplication record in RDS (C-07), so that retried submissions with the same key return the original response without creating duplicate records."
    },
    {

      "question_id": "REL06",
      "question": "REL 6. How do you monitor workload resources?",

      "finding": "CloudWatch alarms are defined but the design does not describe any automated response actions attached to them; all alarm responses appear to require manual operator intervention.",
      "recommendation": "Configure an ECS Application Auto Scaling policy triggered by the ALB RequestCountPerTarget metric so that the ECS service automatically adds tasks when request rate rises, providing automated response to load-driven impairment."

      "question_id": "REL07",
      "question": "REL 7. How do you design your workload to adapt to changes in demand?",
      "title": "Obtain resources upon detection of impairment to a workload",

      "finding": "The ECS service can scale to additional tasks (ADR-001) but the design does not describe a reactive scaling policy triggered by an availability impairment alarm (e.g., high error rate or task health check failure).",
      "recommendation": "Define an ECS Application Auto Scaling step scaling policy on the ALB HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count metric to add a task when the 5xx error rate exceeds a threshold, enabling reactive recovery from partial task failure."

    {

      "pillar": "Reliability",
      "question_id": "REL07",
      "question": "REL 7. How do you design your workload to adapt to changes in demand?",

      "recommendation": "Add an ECS Application Auto Scaling target tracking policy on ALB RequestCountPerTarget (target 500 requests/task) with a minimum of 1 and maximum of 4 tasks to automatically provision capacity as demand grows."

    {

      "pillar": "Reliability",
      "question_id": "REL10",
      "question": "REL 10. How do you use fault isolation to protect your workload?",
      "title": "Automate recovery for components constrained to a single location",

      "issue_risk": "Low",
      "status": "partial",
      "scope": "workload",
      "evidence_ids": [
        "C-07",
        "C-10",
        "ADR-007",
        "REQ-12"
      ],
      "finding": "All components are constrained to us-east-1a; the design describes a snapshot-restore recovery path (ADR-007) but does not document a complete, tested rebuild runbook that achieves the 8-hour RTO for a full AZ failure.",
      "recommendation": "Author and include in the design a step-by-step recovery runbook (as an SSM Automation document) covering RDS snapshot restore, ECS service re-registration, and ALB target group validation, with a documented test schedule to validate the 8-hour RTO."
    },
    {
      "bp_id": "REL11-BP05",
      "pillar": "Reliability",
      "question_id": "REL11",
      "question": "REL 11. How do you design your workload to withstand component failures?",
      "title": "Use static stability to prevent bimodal behavior",
      "risk": "Medium",
      "issue_risk": "Low",
      "status": "partial",
      "scope": "workload",
      "evidence_ids": [
        "C-04",
        "REQ-11"
      ],
      "finding": "The single Fargate task (C-04) is sized for normal load; under a failure scenario where the task restarts, it must handle the same load with no pre-provisioned headroom, potentially exhibiting bimodal behavior during recovery.",
      "recommendation": "Set the ECS service desired count to 2 tasks (or configure a minimum of 2 in the auto-scaling policy) so that one task can absorb traffic while the other restarts, eliminating the bimodal recovery window."
    },
    {

      "pillar": "Security",

      "question": "SEC 4. How do you detect and investigate security events?",

      "recommendation": "Add an AWS Config rule with an SSM Automation remediation document to automatically revert unauthorized security group changes on the RDS instance (C-07) and re-enable S3 Block Public Access on C-08 if disabled."

      "recommendation": "Add VPC interface endpoints for Secrets Manager and Cognito (in addition to the existing S3 gateway endpoint) so that all outbound API traffic from the Fargate task stays within the VPC and is subject to endpoint policies rather than traversing the NAT Gateway uncontrolled."

      "question": "SUS 2. How do you align cloud resources to your demand?",
      "title": "Scale workload infrastructure dynamically",
      "risk": "Medium",
      "issue_risk": "Low",
      "status": "partial",
      "scope": "workload",
      "evidence_ids": [
        "C-04",
        "ADR-001"
      ],
      "finding": "The Fargate task runs at a fixed desired count of 1 with no auto-scaling policy defined, meaning the workload cannot scale down during off-hours (nights, weekends) to reduce resource consumption.",
      "recommendation": "Define an ECS Application Auto Scaling policy with a minimum of 1 task so the service can scale down to the minimum during off-hours, and consider an EventBridge Scheduler to set desired count to 0 outside business hours if the 99.0% availability target permits."

    {
      "bp_id": "SUS02-BP06",
      "pillar": "Sustainability",
      "question_id": "SUS02",
      "question": "SUS 2. How do you align cloud resources to your demand?",
      "title": "Implement buffering or throttling to flatten the demand curve",
      "risk": "Low",
      "issue_risk": "Low",
      "status": "partial",
      "scope": "workload",
      "evidence_ids": [

      ],
      "finding": "Email notifications are dispatched synchronously on every status change without any buffering; during burst periods (e.g., bulk status updates by maintenance staff), this creates unnecessary peak load on both the Fargate task and SES.",
      "recommendation": "Decouple notification dispatch by writing pending notifications to a lightweight queue (e.g., an RDS pending_notifications table polled by a scheduled task) so that burst status updates are smoothed before SES delivery."

    {
      "bp_id": "SUS03-BP01",
      "pillar": "Sustainability",
      "question_id": "SUS03",
      "question": "SUS 3. How do you take advantage of software and architecture patterns to support your sustainability goals?",
      "title": "Optimize software and architecture for asynchronous and scheduled jobs",

      "scope": "workload",
      "evidence_ids": [

      "finding": "Notifications are dispatched synchronously within the request-handling path rather than as a scheduled or asynchronous job, preventing efficient resource utilization during burst periods.",
      "recommendation": "Move notification dispatch to an asynchronous path (e.g., a short-interval EventBridge Scheduler polling a pending_notifications table) to decouple notification throughput from the synchronous request-handling path."
